title: TECTONIC CAD: Pivotal IDE Evaluation of Coronary Intravascular Lithotripsy for Severely Calcified Lesions.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Left atrial appendage occlusion (LAAO) is a stroke prevention alternative for patients with atrial fibrillation (AF) intolerant to long-term oral anticoagulation (OAC). The next-generation dual-seal device was designed to improve operator ease of use while maintaining effective LAAO of the predicate device.
OBJECTIVES: The purpose of this analysis was to evaluate the safety and effectiveness of a next-generation device through 1 year.
METHODS: VERITAS is a single-arm, prospective, global, multicenter study. Patients with nonvalvular AF with an increased thromboembolism risk seeking a nonpharmacologic alternative to OAC were enrolled. One-year descriptive endpoints are provided, including mortality, neurological events, major bleeding, and device-related complications. One-year cardiac imaging was assessed for peridevice leak and device-related thrombus (DRT).
RESULTS: Complete left atrial appendage (LAA) closure (0 mm leak) was observed in 91.1% (95% CI: 87.9%-93.7%) of patients by either transesophageal echocardiography (TEE) or cardiac computed tomography and 96.3% (95% CI: 93.2%-98.2%) by TEE alone. The cumulative DRT rate was 3.3% (95% CI: 2.0%-5.3%) with only 0.4% (95% CI: 0.1%-1.5%) deemed clinically relevant. One-year key clinical outcome rates are as follows: all-cause mortality: 3.9% (95% CI: 2.4%-6.3%); cardiovascular mortality: 1.9% (95% CI: 0.9%-3.8%); major bleeding: 6.6% (95% CI: 4.5%-9.2%); ischemic stroke or systemic embolism: 1.8% (95% CI: 0.8%-3.3%); pericardial effusion requiring intervention: 0.9% (95% CI: 0.3%-2.1%). No (0%) device embolization occurred. Median follow-up was 365 days (IQR: 349-380 days).
CONCLUSIONS: The VERITAS study results support the 1-year safety and effectiveness of the next-generation device. (Abbott Medical-VERITAS Study; NCT06707688).
title: 1-Year Safety and Effectiveness of a Next-Generation Dual-Seal Left Atrial Appendage Occluder.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Optimal lesion preparation for coronary calcified nodules (CNs) and intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) pulse delivery for severe calcification remain uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: This study sought to evaluate phenotype-specific calcium modification in severe calcification with and without CNs.
METHODS: In this single-center randomized trial using a new-generation coronary IVL catheter, patients with optical coherence tomography-defined CNs (Cohort A) were assigned 1:1 to rotational atherectomy (RA) plus IVL or IVL alone; patients with severe calcification without CNs (Cohort B) were assigned 1:1 to maximum or operator-determined IVL pulses. Primary endpoints were minimum stent area (MSA) at the CN site in Cohort A and at the maximum calcium arc site in Cohort B.
RESULTS: Among 120 patients, 66 (55%) were in Cohort A (33 per group) and 54 (45%) in Cohort B (27 per group). MSA at the CN site was 7.41 ± 2.12 mm2 with RA plus IVL vs 6.23 ± 1.55 mm2 with IVL alone (mean difference: 1.18 mm2; 95% CI: 0.27-2.09; P = 0.012). In Cohort B, MSA at the maximum calcium arc site was 5.50 ± 1.19 mm2 with maximum IVL pulses vs 5.56 ± 1.45 mm2 with operator-determined IVL pulses (mean difference: -0.06 mm2; 95% CI: -0.78 to 0.67; P = 0.873).
CONCLUSIONS: RA plus IVL increased final stent area vs IVL alone in CN lesions, whereas maximum IVL pulses did not significantly increase final stent area compared with operator-determined pulses in severe calcification without CNs. These findings warrant validation in larger multicenter trials with clinical endpoints. (Coronary Calcified Nodule Management With Rotational Atherectomy Plus Shockwave Intravascular Lithotripsy vs Intravascular Lithotripsy Alone: A Prospective, Randomized Trial [NODULE-SHOCK]; ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT07000045).
title: Rotational Atherectomy Plus Intravascular Lithotripsy Versus Intravascular Lithotripsy Alone for Coronary Calcified Nodules: The NODULE-SHOCK Trial.

abstract: The only treatment of severe aortic stenosis (AS) is aortic valve replacement. No medical therapy has been proven effective for preventing or delaying AS progression despite several clinical trials. The EVOID-AS trial is designed to evaluate the efficacy of evogliptin, a dipeptidyl peptidase 4 inhibitor, at retarding the progression of aortic valve calcification and AS hemodynamic severity in patients with mild to moderate AS. In this trial, 580 patients with mild or moderate native calcific AS at 40+ clinical sites across the United States and Canada will be randomized in a 1:1 allocation to receive either evogliptin 10 mg or placebo once daily orally for 2 years. Clinical follow-up visits are scheduled at 3-month intervals; transthoracic echocardiography, aortic valve computed tomography calcium score, and laboratory testing are obtained at baseline, 1-year, and 2-year study visits. The primary end point is change in aortic valve calcification as measured by cardiac computed tomography at 2 years of therapy. Secondary end points are progression of AS hemodynamic severity by echocardiography during 2 years of therapy and time to aortic valve intervention. Secondary safety end points include incidence and severity of treatment-emergent or serious adverse events. Enrollment began in June 2022, and the study is expected to be completed in 2028. EVOID-AS is a double-blind, placebo-controlled, randomized medical trial to modify the progression of calcific AS. This trial will contribute to the critical unmet clinical need of identifying an effective medical therapy to prevent or to delay the progression of AS. TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT05143177.
title: Efficacy and Safety of Evogliptin in Mild to Moderate Calcific Aortic Valve Stenosis: The EVOID-AS Trial Rationale and Study Design.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Angina is commonly associated with atherosclerotic epicardial coronary artery disease, but it could be the presenting symptom of a coronary structural anomaly or even a noncoronary cardiac structural pathology.
CASE SUMMARY: A 40-year-old man with obesity, hypertension, and hyperlipidemia presented with exertional chest pain and dyspnea. Coronary computed tomographic angiography showed no coronary atherosclerosis. However, there was an absence of a direct left main coronary artery connection to the aortic root, and retrograde filling of the left coronary system from right coronary collateral vessels. Stress echocardiography demonstrated no wall motion abnormality or ventricular arrhythmia. Medical management, including beta-blockade, aggressive risk factor modification, and surveillance, was pursued through shared decision-making.
DISCUSSION: Left main coronary artery atresia is an exceedingly rare congenital anomaly that may present as exertional angina mimicking atherosclerotic coronary artery disease. Coronary computed tomographic angiography provides precise anatomical information for the diagnosis, and functional testing helps guide individualized management.
title: Left Main Coronary Artery Atresia: Chest Pain From an Uncommon Cause.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Marbach-Rustad progeroid syndrome results from the recurrent heterozygous LEMD2 c.1436C>T (p.Ser479Phe) variant. Four cases have been reported, with cardiac involvement absent or only qualitatively described.
CASE SUMMARY: A 30-year-old man with short stature, skeletal fragility, and facial dysmorphism presented with syncope from high-grade atrioventricular block. Echocardiography showed premature severe calcific aortic stenosis and mild mitral stenosis. Cardiac magnetic resonance showed preserved biventricular function with no late gadolinium enhancement; computed tomography confirmed valvular calcification but no coronary calcium. Chagas serology was negative. Whole-genome sequencing confirmed the p.Ser479Phe variant. He received a permanent pacemaker and, 6 months later, transcatheter aortic valve replacement. Evaluation also revealed overt type 2 diabetes, severe hypertriglyceridemia, and nephropathy: the most advanced metabolic phenotype reported.
DISCUSSION: This case shows that the p.Ser479Phe variant can cause advanced, intervention-requiring cardiovascular disease (objectively quantified and, to our knowledge, the first in vivo characterization by cardiac magnetic resonance). These findings support routine cardiac and metabolic surveillance in LEMD2-associated progeroid syndromes.
title: Advanced Cardiovascular Disease in Marbach-Rustad Progeroid Syndrome (LEMD2 p.Ser479Phe).

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Descending necrotizing mediastinitis (DNM) is a rare, life-threatening infection (mortality 18%-36%) that can extend to the pericardium and produce electrocardiogram changes mimicking ST-segmentelevation myocardial infarction (STEMI).
CASE SUMMARY: A young, previously healthy man presented with anterior chest pain. Initial electrocardiogram showed ST-segment elevation prompting STEMI suspicion. Computed tomography angiography of the chest revealed deep neck infection with mediastinal and pericardial extension, diagnosing DNM. Cultures grew Streptococcus constellatus. Management included broad-spectrum intravenous antibiotics and surgical drainage/debridement with intensive care unit care; the patient recovered.
DISCUSSION: DNM arises from oropharyngeal or odontogenic infection spreading along cervical fascial planes, with mortality driven by diagnostic delay and inadequate source control. S constellatus is an uncommon cause. This case highlights pericardial involvement as a noncoronary cause of ST elevation.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Consider noncoronary causes of ST-segment elevation; early imaging is essential to diagnose DNM and guide lifesaving source control.
title: ST-Segment Elevation Beyond the Coronaries: A Case of Necrotizing Mediastinitis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acquired Gerbode defects after transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) are rare and may present atypically, delaying diagnosis.
CASE SUMMARY: A 71-year-old man presented 15 days after TAVR with severe acute liver and kidney injury despite preserved ventricular systolic function and normal prosthetic valve function on transthoracic echocardiography. Right heart catheterization revealed elevated filling pressures, an oxygen saturation step-up from the superior vena cava (51%) to the pulmonary artery (79%), and a pulmonary/systemic flow ratio of 2.9. Transesophageal echocardiography identified a high-pressure left ventricular-to-right atrial shunt through the membranous septum. Residual shunting after transcatheter closure caused severe intravascular hemolysis and necessitated surgical salvage. The postoperative course was complicated by multiorgan failure and death.
DISCUSSION: This case highlights an atypical presentation of an acquired Gerbode defect. Complementary transesophageal echocardiography and invasive hemodynamic assessment were essential for diagnosis.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Occult intracardiac shunting should be considered after TAVR when severe end-organ dysfunction is discordant with reassuring transthoracic echocardiographic findings.
title: Acquired Gerbode Defect After TAVR Presenting With Severe Acute Liver and Kidney Injury.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Shock in sepsis is predominantly vasodilatory; however, concomitant myocardial dysfunction may result in superimposed cardiogenic shock and a mixed shock state.
CASE SUMMARY: A 75-year-old man with Parkinson disease, severe constipation, and stercoral colitis presented with profound shock after an enema. Echocardiography showed new biventricular dysfunction with regional wall-motion abnormalities. Invasive hemodynamic assessment demonstrated elevated filling pressures, low cardiac index, and low systemic vascular resistance despite substantial vasoactive and inotropic support, consistent with a mixed vasodilatory and cardiogenic shock. He improved after antibiotics and vasoactive support, but manual disimpaction after stabilization was followed within minutes by recurrent/similar shock.
REVIEW SUMMARY: This case illustrates a practical approach to mixed shock with acute myocardial dysfunction. Treatment of underlying infection should occur in parallel with characterization of the hemodynamic phenotype. Serial echocardiography and invasive hemodynamic assessment can identify concomitant vasodilatory and cardiogenic shock and guide circulatory support as shock physiology evolves.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGES: Shock physiology is dynamic. In patients with sepsis, serial clinical, echocardiographic, and hemodynamic reassessment can identify concomitant cardiogenic shock and guide circulatory support.
title: Shock With Acute Myocardial Dysfunction in Stercoral Colitis: Diagnosis and Management.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Myocardial infarction (MI) continues to be a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality. This study evaluated the predictive relationships between Creatine Kinase-MB (CK-MB) and Troponin I/T (cTnI/T), creatine phosphokinase (CPK), and C-reactive protein (CRP) markers to improve clinical interpretation where CK-MB assays are unavailable.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective cohort of 102 first-time MI patients from multiple Saudi hospitals was analyzed. Demographic, biochemical, and clinical data were extracted, and univariable and multivariable linear regressions were performed via R (v4.4.2). Subgroup analyses by age, sex, and body mass index were conducted to explore demographic variations.
RESULTS: Mean CK-MB levels were 60.85 ± 51.69 U/L in males and 53.71 ± 45.44 U/L in females. cTnI/T, averaged 7.87 ± 12.65 ng/mL, total CPK 370.85 ± 466.99 U/L, and CRP 22.09 ± 14.12 mg/L. Univariable regression revealed strong positive association of CK-MB with cTnI/T, (estimate = 2.98, P < 0.0001, R2 = 0.583), CPK (estimate = 0.082, P < 0.0001, R2 = 0.468), and CRP (estimate = 1.67, P < 0.0001, R2 = 0.202). In the multivariable model, cTnI/T (estimate = 2.33, P < 0.0001) and CPK (estimate = 0.047, P < 0.0001) remained independent predictors, while CRP lost significance (P = 0.192).
DISCUSSION AND CONCLUSION: These findings support using cTnI/T and CPK as reliable clinical correlates for CK-MB estimation in post MI evaluation, especially when laboratory access is limited.
title: Clinical predictive modeling of CK-MB using troponin I/T and CPK in patients post myocardial infarction.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) has emerged as a rescue strategy for selected patients with refractory cardiac arrest. However, identifying patients most likely to achieve neurologically meaningful survival remains challenging. Conventional selection criteria, including age, initial rhythm, witnessed arrest, bystander cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR), and no-flow and low-flow duration, are clinically useful but may be insufficient when interpreted as isolated thresholds.
METHODS: We conducted a narrative review of contemporary evidence on ECPR patient selection, incorporating randomized trials, observational studies, registries, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, and current guideline and consensus recommendations. Evidence was critically evaluated with particular attention to patient-level prognostic factors, arrest setting, dynamic physiological and metabolic variables, ECPR logistics, and system-level determinants of outcome.
RESULTS: Current evidence supports a multidimensional rather than single-variable approach to ECPR candidacy. Favorable arrest characteristics, potentially reversible etiology, shorter low-flow duration, and preserved physiological reserve remain important; however, chronological low-flow time should be interpreted alongside the quality and effectiveness of ongoing CPR. Dynamic information-including transient return of spontaneous circulation, lactate kinetics, arterial pH, end-tidal carbon dioxide, and hemodynamic parameters-may further refine assessment of biological viability. Frailty, comorbidity burden, cerebral perfusion, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation-related contraindications should also be incorporated into decision-making. Importantly, selection cannot be separated from system performance: Cannulation strategy, transport logistics, institutional experience, and the ability to establish extracorporeal circulation rapidly may substantially modify the likelihood of benefit. Differences between out-of-hospital and in-hospital cardiac arrest further limit the universal application of rigid eligibility criteria.
CONCLUSION: Candidacy for ECPR should be viewed as a dynamic, probability-based assessment rather than a checklist of fixed thresholds. Integrating arrest characteristics, reversibility, evolving physiology, patient reserve, and system capability may provide a more clinically meaningful framework for identifying patients most likely to achieve neurologically favorable survival after ECPR.
title: Refining ECPR candidate selection: from fixed criteria to a dynamic probability-of-benefit framework.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Aortic root replacement (ARR) can be performed with a stentless porcine xenograft (Freestyle®) as an alternative to the conventional Bentall-procedure, where mechanical or stented bioprosthetic are sewn into a wov-en tube-graft. We examined early and late outcomes of Freestyle®-ARR in a whole-nation cohort, focusing on indications and surgical outcomes.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A retrospective analysis that included 44 consecutive Freestyle®-ARR performed at Landspitali 2002-2018. Primary outcomes were 30-day and long-term survival (Kaplan-Meier), with a median follow-up of 111 months. Secondary outcomes included early postoperative complications and late reoperations.
RESULTS: A median of three cases was performed per year (range 0-5). The most common indication was dilated aortic root (70%), followed by Type-A aortic dissection (9%) and small aortic annulus during aortic valve replacement (9%). Average age was 62 years and 65% were male. Median EuroSCORE-II was 11% (range 3-71%), cardiopulmonary bypass time 234 min. and cross-clamp time 157 min. The most common postoperative complications were new-onset atrial fibrillation (51%) and perioperative myocardial infarction (14%). Postoperative length of stay was 12 days median and 30-day mortality 14% (n=6). At follow-up, 1- and 5-year survival rates were 81% and 74%, respectively. For patients surviving the first 30 days, 5-year survival was 86%, and at long-term follow-up only three patients (7%) had undergone reoperation.
CONCLUSIONS: Freestyle®-ARR is a technically challenging operation and is associated with high short-term mortality rates compared with regular AVR. However, long term survival was favourable, and reoperations were uncommon in those surviving to discharge.

abstract:
IMPORTANCE: Following a left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) procedure, antithrombotic therapy is administered to safely allow time for device endothelialization. However, the optimal postimplant antithrombotic regimen is unknown.
OBJECTIVE: To determine if either reduced-dose non-vitamin K oral anticoagulants (NOACs) or aspirin alone are noninferior to dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) for the composite clinical end point of death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding through 6 months post LAAC.
DESIGN, SETTING, AND PARTICIPANTS: This open-label, 3-group, multicenter clinical trial randomized 1857 patients between October 2024 and December 2025 at 87 US investigational sites, with the final 6-month follow-up in July 2026. Enrolled patients had nonvalvular atrial fibrillation, underwent successful LAAC, and were eligible for all 3 regimens.
INTERVENTIONS: Patients were randomly allocated 1:1:1 to DAPT for 6 months followed by aspirin (n = 624), a reduced-dose NOAC for 3 months followed by aspirin (n = 620), or aspirin alone for 12 months (n = 613).
MAIN OUTCOMES AND MEASURES: The primary outcome was the 6-month composite of all-cause death, stroke, systemic embolism, or major bleeding. Noninferiority was tested in the primary analysis population with a 1-sided Farrington-Manning test (α = .025). Bleeding and 45-day device-related thrombus rates were exploratory without multiplicity adjustment.
RESULTS: The cohort had a mean age of 76 (SD, 8) years, 42.9% were female, the mean CHA2DS2-VASc score was 4.2 (SD, 1.3), and 68.0% had paroxysmal atrial fibrillation. The primary outcome occurred in 41 patients (6.9%) with DAPT vs 31 (5.1%) with a reduced-dose NOAC (risk ratio, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.48-1.18]; risk difference, -1.7 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, 1.2) and 20 (3.3%) with aspirin alone (risk ratio, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.29-0.82]; risk difference, -3.5 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, -0.8). Both monotherapy strategies met noninferiority criteria (P < .001 for noninferiority for both). Major bleeding was 4.5% with DAPT, 2.7% with reduced-dose NOACs, and 1.7% with aspirin alone; clinically relevant nonmajor bleeding was 8.7%, 4.8%, and 3.8%, respectively. Device-related thrombus was observed in 3.4%, 0.9%, and 2.7%, respectively.
CONCLUSIONS AND RELEVANCE: Both reduced-dose NOACs and aspirin alone were noninferior to DAPT for 6-month outcomes after uncomplicated LAAC.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: ClinicalTrials.gov Identifier: NCT06521463.

appraisal.design_and_n: Open-label, 3-group, multicenter clinical trial randomized 1857 patients at 87 US investigational sites: DAPT for 6 months followed by aspirin (n = 624), a reduced-dose NOAC for 3 months followed by aspirin (n = 620), or aspirin alone for 12 months (n = 613).
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label, with a primary outcome limited to 6 months; bleeding and device-related thrombus rates were exploratory without multiplicity adjustment, and all sites were in the US.
appraisal.one_line: Reduced-dose NOAC and aspirin alone were each noninferior to dual antiplatelet therapy for the 6-month composite after left atrial appendage closure, with aspirin alone showing the lowest event rate.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: The primary outcome occurred in 41 patients (6.9%) with DAPT vs 31 (5.1%) with a reduced-dose NOAC (risk ratio, 0.75 [95% CI, 0.48-1.18]; risk difference, -1.7 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, 1.2) and 20 (3.3%) with aspirin alone (risk ratio, 0.49 [95% CI, 0.29-0.82]; risk difference, -3.5 percentage points; 97.5% upper bound, -0.8). Both monotherapy strategies met noninferiority criteria (P < .001 for noninferiority for both).
appraisal.why_it_matters: Addresses a regimen question with no settled answer after left atrial appendage closure and supports simpler, less bleeding-prone antithrombotic therapy, with direct relevance to guideline wording and to evidence synthesis on post-implant regimens.

title: Antithrombotic Therapy After Left Atrial Appendage Occlusion: The SIMPLAAFY Randomized Clinical Trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: For patients with moderate aortic stenosis, current guidelines recommend clinical surveillance with echocardiographic assessment every 1 or 2 years. Whether transcatheter aortic-valve replacement (TAVR) will improve outcomes in these patients remains unknown.
METHODS: We conducted an international, open-label, randomized trial to evaluate whether TAVR will result in better outcomes than clinical surveillance among patients with moderate aortic stenosis with at least one at-risk feature (i.e., a symptom or structural or functional abnormality that has been shown to be associated with faster disease progression or adverse cardiovascular outcomes). The patients were assigned in a 1:1 ratio to undergo transfemoral TAVR with a balloon-expandable valve or clinical surveillance. The primary effectiveness end point was a composite of death from any cause or a heart-failure event with or without hospitalization at 2 years. Superiority testing was performed in the intention-to-treat population.
RESULTS: A total of 744 patients underwent randomization: 373 patients were assigned to the TAVR group and 371 to the clinical-surveillance group. The mean age of patients was 78 years, 39.1% were women, and 45.6% were at low surgical risk. The mean aortic-valve area was 1.2 cm2, and the mean aortic-valve peak velocity was 3.3 m per second. At 2 years, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients with a primary effectiveness end-point event was 16.7% in the TAVR group and 23.9% in the clinical-surveillance group (risk difference, -7.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -13.1 to -1.3; P = 0.02 for superiority). The Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients who died from any cause was 8.4% in the TAVR group and 7.3% in the clinical-surveillance group; the estimates for a heart-failure event were 10.8% and 19.0%, respectively. The incidence of procedure-related adverse events did not differ meaningfully between the patients in the TAVR group and those in the clinical-surveillance group who underwent aortic-valve replacement.
CONCLUSIONS: Among patients with moderate aortic stenosis and at-risk features, a strategy of TAVR was superior to clinical surveillance in lowering the incidence of death or a heart-failure event at 2 years. (Funded by Edwards Lifesciences; PROGRESS ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT04889872.).

appraisal.design_and_n: International, open-label, randomized trial; 744 patients underwent randomization: 373 patients were assigned to the TAVR group and 371 to the clinical-surveillance group.
appraisal.main_limitation: Open-label; the composite includes heart-failure events with or without hospitalisation, which are open to ascertainment bias, and all-cause death did not differ (8.4% vs 7.3%); industry funded, with a 2-year horizon and no data on valve durability.
appraisal.one_line: TAVR with a balloon-expandable valve reduced death or heart-failure events at 2 years compared with clinical surveillance in moderate aortic stenosis with at-risk features.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 2 years, the Kaplan-Meier estimate of the percentage of patients with a primary effectiveness end-point event was 16.7% in the TAVR group and 23.9% in the clinical-surveillance group (risk difference, -7.2 percentage points; 95% confidence interval, -13.1 to -1.3; P = 0.02 for superiority).
appraisal.why_it_matters: First randomised evidence for intervention before severe stenosis, in a population for which guidelines currently recommend surveillance, and so a direct challenge to current recommendations and timing of aortic valve intervention.

journal: The New England journal of medicine
title: TAVR in Patients with Moderate Aortic Stenosis with At-Risk Features.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Frailty results from declining reserve and function and is a modifiable cardiovascular risk-factor. Despite this, there is limited evidence surrounding its role in lower-risk TAVR cohorts.
OBJECTIVES: This study aimed to evaluate frailty among contemporary TAVR patients, delineate the impact of biochemical and clinical frailty, and understand its additive value to existing risk-prediction tools.
METHODS: Analysis of a multicenter Australian registry. Biochemical frailty (BF) was defined as serum albumin <35 g/L and clinical frailty (CF) as a Rockwood Clinical Frailty Scale ≥5. Patients meeting BF or CF criteria were categorized as frail.
RESULTS: Of the 2,661 patients, the median age 82 (IQR: 77-86), 60% male, and median STS 3.3 (2-5.2), 920 patients (35%) were considered frail. A total of 171 (19%) of frail patients fulfilled both BF and CF criteria. The frail group was older (83 vs 81, P < 0.001), more females (43% vs 38%; P = 0.016) with higher STS scores (4 vs 3, P < 0.001). Kaplan-Meier analysis showed a stepwise increase in 12-month mortality with increasing frailty (no frailty 4% vs BF or CF 7% vs BF + CF 16%, Log-rank P < 0.001). In Cox proportional hazards regression BF or CF (adjusted HR: 1.6; 95% CI: 1.0-2.4; P = 0.033) and BF + CF (adjusted HR: 3.3; 95% CI: 1.9-5.6; P < 0.001) independently predicted 12-month mortality. Addition of frailty to STS Score improved mortality prediction (area under the receiver-operating characteristic curve: 0.608 vs 0.664; DeLong's P = 0.021), with Shapley analysis demonstrating significant contribution from frailty.
CONCLUSIONS: Frailty is common with significant implications in TAVR. Patients with biochemical and clinical frailty criteria are highest risk. Development of strategies to address frailty is critical.
title: The Impact of Clinical and Biochemical Frailty on Outcomes following Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: High thrombus burden in ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is associated with impaired reperfusion and adverse outcomes. We aimed to develop and internally validate an admission-only, β-weighted electrocardiographic (ECG) score for pre-angiographic identification of high thrombus burden in young patients with STEMI.
METHODS: This retrospective single-center study included 761 patients aged ≤45 years undergoing primary PCI. High thrombus burden was defined as TIMI thrombus grade 4-5. The 0-7-point ECG score comprised reciprocal ST-segment depression (1 point), terminal QRS distortion (2 points), fragmented QRS (2 points), and frontal QRS-T angle >90° (2 points). Internal validation was performed using 1000 bootstrap resamples.
RESULTS: High thrombus burden was present in 349 patients. The ECG score was higher in the high-thrombus-burden group than in the low-thrombus-burden group (3 [2-5] vs. 1 [0-2]; p < 0.001). The β-weighted ECG score showed an apparent AUC of 0.769 and an optimism-corrected AUC of 0.758. At a cut-off of ≥3 points, sensitivity was 65.6% and specificity was 80.1%.
CONCLUSION: An admission-only β-weighted ECG score provided useful pre-angiographic discrimination of high thrombus burden without requiring laboratory results. Prospective external validation is required before routine clinical implementation.
STUDY PERIOD: This retrospective observational study included young patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction who underwent emergent coronary angiography and primary percutaneous coronary intervention between June 2014 and June 2025.
title: β-weighted admission ECG score for pre-angiographic prediction of high thrombus burden in young STEMI: Development and internal validation.

abstract: Cardiac arrest (CA) complicating cardiogenic shock (CS) identifies a high-risk phenotype, but population-level mortality trends among patients with both conditions are not well described. Using the CDC WONDER Multiple Cause of Death database, we identified deaths among US adults aged ≥25 years from 1999 to 2024 in which both CA (ICD-10 I46) and CS (R57.0) were recorded on the same death certificate and compared them with all CS-related deaths. Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per 100,000 population were calculated, and temporal trends were assessed using Joinpoint regression. Overall, 98,531 CA+CS deaths occurred, compared with 577,658 CS-related deaths. The AAMR for CA+CS declined from 1.3 in 1999 to 0.9 in the mid-2000s, rose by 10.1% per year between 2009 and 2021 (95% CI 9.8 to 10.5) to a peak of 2.9, and declined modestly to 2.7 by 2024. The share of CS deaths that also listed CA increased from 12.4% to 18.9%. Men had consistently higher AAMRs than women (3.6 vs 1.9 in 2024), and adults aged ≥65 years accounted for 71.3% of deaths. Non-Hispanic Black adults had the highest rates from 2016 onward and the steepest increase, while the West had the highest and the Midwest the lowest rates among census regions. CA+CS mortality in the United States has roughly doubled since 1999, with persistent differences by sex, race and ethnicity, age, and region that warrant study with clinically detailed data.
title: Trends and disparities in mortality related to cardiac arrest and cardiogenic shock: A 1999-2024 United States analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Guidelines favor surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR) in patients aged 65 years or younger with aortic stenosis, yet many receive transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) without supportive data. We performed a target trial emulation of SAVR versus TAVI in this population.
METHODS: Using the all-payer Premier Healthcare Database (2016-2024), patients aged 50 to 65 years undergoing isolated SAVR or TAVI within 90 days of an aortic stenosis diagnosis were evaluated. After trial exclusions, frailty and predicted risk were incorporated into a clone-censor-weight framework with inverse probability weighting. Reporting adhered to TARGET guidance. The primary outcome was the 5-year composite of all-cause mortality, stroke, valve reintervention, or heart failure rehospitalization.
RESULTS: The clone-censor-weighted analysis included 18,549 SAVR and 18,549 TAVI patients, balanced across all covariates (standardized mean difference <0.10). Mean age was 60 years, and many were of low surgical risk <4% (SAVR 69.5% vs TAVI 49.7%). In-hospital mortality (0.41% vs 0.31%; odds ratio, 0.61; p<0.001) and periprocedural stroke (0.31% vs 0.28%; odds ratio, 0.67; p<0.001) favored TAVI. At 5 years, risk-adjusted freedom from the primary composite outcome (87.5% vs 77.8%; hazard ratio, 1.87; p<0.001), heart failure rehospitalization (92.9% vs 88.2%; subdistribution hazard ratio, 1.72; p<0.001), and all-cause mortality (93.6% vs 85.6%; hazard ratio, 2.34; p<0.001) favored SAVR.
CONCLUSIONS: For contemporary patients aged 50 to 65 years, the primary composite outcome favored SAVR over TAVI at 5 years, most markedly at centers with high young TAVI utilization. These data may guide heart team decision making and future trial design.

appraisal.design_and_n: Target trial emulation using the all-payer Premier Healthcare Database (2016-2024); the clone-censor-weighted analysis included 18,549 SAVR and 18,549 TAVI patients aged 50 to 65 years.
appraisal.main_limitation: Administrative hospital data with possible residual confounding, limited anatomical and imaging detail, and follow-up that depends on return to the database's hospitals.
appraisal.one_line: In a target trial emulation of patients aged 50 to 65 years, SAVR was associated with better 5-year composite outcomes than TAVI.
appraisal.primary_result_as_reported: At 5 years, risk-adjusted freedom from the primary composite outcome (87.5% vs. 77.8%; hazard ratio, 1.87; p<0.001), heart failure rehospitalization (92.9% vs. 88.2%; subdistribution hazard ratio, 1.72; p<0.001), and all-cause mortality (93.6% vs. 85.6%; hazard ratio, 2.34; p<0.001) favored SAVR. The abstract gives p-values but no confidence intervals.
appraisal.why_it_matters: Provides observational comparative data in an age group where TAVI is used without trial support and where guidelines favour surgery, and illustrates a target trial emulation design in a population excluded from the defining trials.

title: Aortic Valve Replacement in Patients 50-65 Years: A Target Trial Emulation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The clinical meaning of post-resuscitation ST-segment elevation in out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA) patients with suspected coronary etiology remains uncertain. We aimed to describe coronary angiographic phenotypes and clinical outcomes according to post-resuscitation ST-segment findings in an angiography-evaluable subset of OHCA survivors with presumed coronary lesion-related arrest.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed 149 successfully resuscitated OHCA patients admitted to our institution between January 2015 and December 2023, who underwent post-resuscitation coronary angiography and had presumed culprit lesions, defined by integrating angiographic findings with electrocardiographic, echocardiographic, and biomarker data in the clinical context. Patients were classified according to the presence or absence of post-resuscitation ST-segment elevation.
RESULTS: ST-segment elevation was associated with a more acute occlusive coronary phenotype, with more impaired culprit-vessel flow and greater myocardial injury. In contrast, patients without ST-segment elevation more frequently had multivessel disease and chronic total occlusion, suggesting more complex coronary artery disease. Favorable neurological outcome was less frequent with ST-segment elevation in unadjusted analyses, but this association was not independent of pre-hospital factors.
CONCLUSIONS: In this selected OHCA subset, post-resuscitation ST-segment elevation was associated with an acute occlusive coronary phenotype and greater myocardial injury, as in non-arrest acute coronary syndromes. However, the absence of ST-segment elevation did not exclude a coronary culprit lesion, so comprehensive coronary assessment is essential. ST-segment elevation was not independently associated with clinical outcomes after adjustment for pre-hospital factors. These findings should be interpreted considering substantial selection inherent to the study population.
title: Post-resuscitation ST-segment elevation and coronary angiographic phenotypes in angiography-evaluable survivors of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest with presumed coronary lesion-related arrest.

abstract: Randomized trials have shown short-term benefit of extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) for refractory out-of-hospital cardiac arrest (OHCA), but the long-term durability of survival and neurological recovery after hospital discharge remains poorly defined. We performed a retrospective cohort study of consecutive patients discharged alive after ECPR for refractory VT/VF OHCA from two academic centers (University of Minnesota, USA, and Charles University, Prague) from January 2013 through December 2022. The primary outcome was 5-year survival. Secondary outcomes included neurological status by Cerebral Performance Category (CPC) and associations of age and discharge disposition with long-term outcomes. Among 728 patients treated with ECPR, 211 (29.0%) survived to discharge; 138 from Minnesota and 73 from Prague. Median follow-up was 3.9 years; 68 patients (32%) completed 5 years. No patients were lost to follow-up. Among hospital survivors, 76.9% and 67.2% were alive at 1 and 5 years, respectively, with most deaths occurring within 90 days of discharge. CPC 1-2 was present in 78.7% at discharge and remained high among survivors beyond 1 year (93.4%-94.2%). Five-year survival declined by age from 91.6% for those between 18-39 years to 52.9% for >70 years. Discharge disposition also strongly stratified long-term prognosis. Among patients discharged alive after ECPR for refractory OHCA, long-term survival was substantial, with approximately two-thirds alive at 5 years with favorable CPC in most. Younger age and discharge home or to acute rehabilitation identified subgroups with particularly favorable prognosis. These findings support the long-term durability of benefit among selected patients treated within established ECPR systems of care.
title: Long-Term Survival Following Extracorporeal Cardiopulmonary Resuscitation: A Two-Center Five-Year Analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND AND AIMS: Patients with anatomically complex coronary artery disease may be considered more suitable for coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) than percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), but some undergo PCI because of clinical constraints and experience higher long-term cardiovascular risk. The physiological rationale underlying this excess post-PCI risk remains unclear. From the perspective of post-PCI revascularization completeness and physiological results, we sought to explain the drivers of excess long-term adverse risk among patients with Favor CABG anatomy undergoing PCI.
METHODS: Coronary physiology based on quantitative flow ratio (QFR) was retrospectively evaluated in the randomized PANDA III trial in which all patients underwent PCI. Patients were stratified into 2 predefined groups by baseline SYNTAX score: Favor PCI or Favor CABG. Functional revascularization completeness was assessed using classic residual functional SYNTAX score (c-rFSS). Final physiological results were quantified by post-PCI QFR. Causal mediation analyses used 2-year major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) excluding periprocedural MI as the outcome to estimate the proportion of the group-outcome association statistically accounted for by residual coronary physiological profiles. The primary endpoint was 2-year MACE, defined as the composite of all-cause death, all MI, or any ischemia-driven revascularization.
RESULTS: A total of 1555 patients with complete post-PCI physiological assessment constituted the final study cohort, among whom 269 (17.3%) individuals were stratified to Favor CABG group by baseline SYNTAX score. The 2-year MACE rate was significantly higher in the Favor CABG than the Favor PCI group (18.6% vs 9.2%; adjusted HR: 1.78; 95% CI: 1.27-2.50). Functional incomplete revascularization (c-rFSS >0) was substantially more prevalent among patients in the Favor CABG group (53.2% vs. 15.1%, P < 0.001). Suboptimal post-PCI physiology defined by QFR <0.90 was more frequent in Favor CABG cohort (32.0% vs 11.8%, P < 0.001). In analyses using MACE excluding periprocedural MI, the estimated proportions mediated by functional incomplete revascularization and suboptimal post-PCI physiology were 49.4% and 47.8%, respectively, and their estimated joint proportion mediated was 79.8%. Integrating c-rFSS or post-PCI QFR into clinical-anatomic risk models significantly improved discrimination and reclassification capacity for 2-year MACE (all P < 0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: In this post hoc analysis of an all-comers PCI trial, approximately one-fifth of patients presented with anatomic complexity warranting CABG as the preferred revascularization strategy. Favor CABG anatomy was associated with higher 2-year MACE than Favor PCI anatomy. This association may be partly explained by the higher prevalence of residual functional incomplete revascularization and suboptimal post-PCI physiology. These findings between Favor CABG and Favor PCI anatomy do not represent a head-to-head comparison and should not be interpreted as a direct comparison of revascularization modalities.

title: Residual physiological profiles in patients with CABG- or PCI-Favored coronary anatomy: A post hoc analysis of the PANDA III randomized clinical trial.

abstract: Background: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) and coronary calcification increase risk for adverse events following drug-eluting stent (DES) implantation. We evaluated whether outcomes following vessel preparation with orbital atherectomy (OA) versus balloon angioplasty (BA) vary according to CKD. Methods: This pre-specified CKD sub-analysis of the prospective, multicenter ECLIPSE trial evaluated 2,001 patients with severely calcified lesions randomized to OA versus BA prior to DES. Independent predictors of two-year target-vessel failure (TVF)-a composite of cardiac death, target-vessel myocardial infarction (TV-MI), or ischemia-driven target-vessel revascularization (ID-TVR)-were determined using multivariable Cox proportional hazards modeling. Results: CKD (eGFR <60 mL/min/1.73m² or hemodialysis) was present in 694 (34.7%) patients; 112 required hemodialysis. Two-year TVF was significantly higher with versus without CKD (21.2% vs. 11.6%; p<0.001), driven by increased cardiac death and ID-TVR. Hemodialysis independently predicted TVF (adjusted HR 2.14, 95% CI 1.30-3.53; p=0.003), whereas reduced eGFR alone did not (p=0.070). In patients on hemodialysis, OA versus BA was associated with higher rates of TVF (52.3% vs. 30.7%; adjusted HR 2.50, 95% CI 1.16-5.41; P=0.020), driven by higher rates of TV-MI and ID-TVR, whereas TVF was similar after OA versus BA in patients not on hemodialysis (13.5% vs. 13.1%; adjusted HR 1.05, 95% CI 0.81-1.35; P=0.730); however, the interaction between treatment assignment and hemodialysis status was not significant (Pint=0.244). Conclusions: CKD remains a major predictor of adverse outcomes after DES implantation in severely calcified lesions, with the highest risks in patients on hemodialysis. In the ECLIPSE trial, higher two-year rates of TVF were observed after vessel preparation with OA compared with BA in patients on hemodialysis but not in patients with CKD not on hemodialysis or in those without CKD. Given the modest hemodialysis subgroup size and non-significant interaction testing, confirmation of these findings in additional studies is warranted.
title: Impact of CKD and Hemodialysis on Treatment of Severely Calcified Lesions: The ECLIPSE Trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Proton pump inhibitors are often prescribed with aspirin and clopidogrel to reduce gastrointestinal bleeding risk. However, the European Society of Cardiology diabetes guidelines recommend avoiding concomitant use of omeprazole and clopidogrel due to potential drug–drug interactions. Evidence in patients with diabetes mellitus (DM), who have a higher prevalence of high on-treatment platelet reactivity, remains limited. In Thailand, where omeprazole is the only reimbursed PPI, this potential interaction has important clinical implications. We aimed to evaluate the effect of omeprazole on platelet reactivity, measured as P2Y12 reaction units (PRU), in patients with DM and coronary artery disease (CAD) receiving aspirin and clopidogrel.
METHODS: This double-blind, randomised, placebo-controlled crossover trial enrolled patients with DM and CAD receiving aspirin 81 mg/day and clopidogrel 75 mg/day. Participants received omeprazole 20 mg or a matching placebo for 2 weeks, followed by crossover to the alternate treatment. Platelet reactivity was assessed using the VerifyNow P2Y12 assay. The primary outcome was the change in PRU following omeprazole coadministration compared with both baseline and placebo. Secondary outcomes included changes in clopidogrel responder status (PRU >208) before and after omeprazole treatment and PRU values in each treatment period.
RESULTS: 50 patients were enrolled (median age 67 years; 58% male). Omeprazole significantly increased PRU by a mean difference of 20.57 units versus baseline (p=0.002) and 16.14 units versus placebo (p=0.006). The proportion of clopidogrel non-responders increased from 44% to 56%, with 25% of baseline responders converting to non-responders.
CONCLUSIONS: Omeprazole significantly attenuated clopidogrel’s antiplatelet effect in patients with diabetes and CAD. Concomitant use may be avoided, especially in those with high thrombotic risk.
TRIAL REGISTRATION NUMBER: TCTR20260714003.
title: Effect of omeprazole on platelet reactivity in patients with diabetes mellitus and coronary artery disease receiving aspirin and clopidogrel: a randomised, placebo-controlled crossover trial (POC-DM).

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To compare the efficacy of intra-operative middle meatus drug-eluting stent implantation versus standalone functional endoscopic sinus surgery (FESS) for chronic rhinosinusitis in subjective symptoms, mucosal morphology and inflammatory factors.
METHODS: Sixty chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps patients (Changsha Central Hospital, January 2023 to June 2024) were assigned to two groups based on voluntary treatment preference: an experimental group with intra-operative stent implantation and a control group with standalone FESS. The Sino-Nasal Outcome Test 22, Lund-Kennedy scores and nasal secretion Matrix Metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) were assessed pre-operatively, and 3 and 12 months post-operatively. Data were analysed by SPSS 27.0 (p < 0.05 for significance).
RESULTS: All indicators decreased post-operatively in both groups (p < 0.05). MMP-9 reduction was similar at 3 months (p > 0.05); at 12 months, the experimental group had greater MMP-9 reduction and more significant decreases in related symptom scores (p < 0.05).
CONCLUSION: Intra-operative middle meatus drug-eluting stent implantation may provide additional benefits compared with standalone FESS in improving subjective symptoms, accelerating nasal mucosal repair and inhibiting inflammation within 12 months of follow up.
journal: The Journal of laryngology and otology
title: Efficacy of sinus drug-eluting stents for chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps: a multidimensional study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute coronary syndrome (ACS) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide. Despite the availability of guideline-directed medical therapy (GDMT), postdischarge continuity of care (CoC) remains suboptimal, and evidence from Asian health-care systems remains limited. The present study examined the association between CoC and clinical outcomes in Taiwanese patients with ACS.
METHODS: This nationwide observational cohort study was conducted using data from Taiwan's National Health Insurance Research Database. It included patients who had their first ACS-related hospitalization between 2012 and 2020 and excluded those who died during the index hospitalization or experienced study outcomes within 1 month after discharge. CoC was assessed in terms of physician, specialty, and GDMT continuity. Study outcomes were all-cause mortality, major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs), hospitalization for heart failure (HHF), and major bleeding.
RESULTS: This study included 140 214 patients with ACS. Patients with low physician continuity had significantly higher risks of all-cause mortality (adjusted risk ratio [aRR]: 2.20, 95% confidence interval [CI] 2.09 to 2.31), cardiovascular death (aRR: 1.97, 95% CI: 1.81 to 2.15), MACEs (aRR: 1.78, 95% CI: 1.66 to 1.90), HHF (aRR: 1.66, 95% CI: 1.54 to 1.78), and major bleeding (aRR: 1.45, 95% CI: 1.26 to 1.66) than did those with high physician continuity. Low specialty continuity was associated with a 1.28-to-1.95-fold increase in the risk of adverse outcomes. Furthermore, low GDMT continuity was significantly associated with elevated risks of all-cause mortality, cardiovascular death, and MACEs but not HHF or major bleeding.
CONCLUSION: The findings suggest that lower CoC during the first year after ACS-related hospitalization is associated with poorer clinical outcomes. Future studies should explore strategies to improve CoC.
journal: Journal of the Chinese Medical Association : JCMA
title: Postdischarge continuity of care and cardiovascular outcomes in acute coronary syndrome.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) is an acute cardiac condition marked by reversible left ventricular dysfunction, with clinical features that resemble acute coronary syndrome but occur without significant coronary artery stenosis. Its development is strongly linked to catecholamine-mediated toxicity. Inflammatory mediators released during allergic responses may further amplify catecholamine secretion; however, drug-induced anaphylactic shock accompanied by TTS has only been rarely documented.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 31-year-old female experienced simultaneous anaphylactic shock and TTS (EF 31%) after receiving intravenous moxifloxacin. Emergency management involved adrenaline, corticosteroids, and antihistamines, together with PICCO-guided circulatory support (target MAP ≥ 65 mmHg) and combined antiplatelet/anticoagulant therapy. A family-based "3-min emergency response" training program and a graded rehabilitation protocol were carried out. Before discharge, ADRB1 genetic testing was completed, which identified the GG genotype, and beta-blocker treatment was then started accordingly. The patient's EF increased to 45% within 48 h, recovered completely within 10 days, and remained stable throughout 6-month pregnancy follow-up under multidisciplinary care, including dynamic EF monitoring ≥ 55% and anticoagulant adjustment.
CONCLUSION: Moxifloxacin may contribute to TTS through allergic-sympathetic pathways, making careful recognition of overlapping symptoms necessary. Important approaches for lowering recurrence risk include family training, gene-guided therapy, and multidisciplinary cooperation. This study offers useful insight into the care of drug-related TTS, highlighting the need for allergy assessment before drug administration and continued follow-up care. This study was approved by the Medical Ethics Committee of Zhejiang Provincial Tongde Hospital (Ethics Approval No: 2025-Research-069), and the patient provided written informed consent for the use of anonymized case data for academic research.
CLINICAL TRIAL NUMBER: MR-33-25-027765.
title: Emergency management and nursing care of a patient with moxifloxacin-induced anaphylactic shock complicated with Takotsubo syndrome.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: In this study, we aimed to explore the relationship between endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) and the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) patients.
METHOD: This retrospective study was based on the clinical data of the AMI patients admitted in emergency department of Changsha Central Hospital from August 2020 to January 2023. Different models were constructed by multivariable regression analysis for investigating the relationship between EASIX index and MACE risk. Restricted cubic spline (RCS) analysis was utilized for further validating the potential nonlinear relationship. The receiver-operator characteristic (ROC) analysis of EASIX index for predicting MACE risk in AMI was done.
RESULTS: 805 AMI patients with 193 individuals in MACE group were included. After adjusting potential confounders, with per unit increasement in EASIX index, the risk of MACE increased by 16% (OR = 1.16, 95%CI: 1.04-1.29, p = 0.0054). The RCS showed the nonlinear relationship between EASIX index and the incidence of MACE was not significant. The predictive performances of EASIX index were showed as follow: an AUC of 0.687 (95%CI:0.642-0.732) and a cut-off value of 2.42.
CONCLUSION: A significant relationship between EASIX index and the incidence of MACE in AMI was identified.
title: The relationship between endothelial activation and stress index (EASIX) and the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events in acute myocardial infarction patients admitted in emergency department.

abstract: Extracorporeal cardiopulmonary resuscitation (ECPR) has emerged as a lifesaving strategy for refractory cardiac arrest, restoring systemic perfusion when conventional cardiopulmonary resuscitation fails. However, ECPR profoundly disrupts haemostasis, driven by the combined effects of whole-body ischaemia-reperfusion injury, systemic inflammation, endothelial activation, platelet dysfunction, and blood contact with extracorporeal surfaces. Together, these processes create a highly dynamic and unstable thromboinflammatory milieu, marked by the simultaneous risk of thrombosis and life-threatening bleeding. Systemic anticoagulation is required to maintain circuit patency and prevent thromboembolic complications, yet optimal strategies remain uncertain. Haemostasis during ECPR is highly dynamic, shaped by the underlying aetiology of cardiac arrest, patient-specific characteristics, and circuit-related factors. This complexity underscores the limitations of fixed anticoagulation targets and the need for individualized, context-sensitive management guided by continuous clinical and laboratory assessment. Despite the increasing global adoption of ECPR, high-quality evidence to guide anticoagulation practices remains scarce. Current strategies are largely extrapolated from other extracorporeal life support populations, contributing to substantial inter-centre variability. This review synthesizes the available evidence on coagulopathy and anticoagulation in adult patients receiving ECPR and discusses emerging approaches to monitoring and anticoagulation management.
title: Coagulopathy and anticoagulation management in adult ECPR patients.

abstract:
AIMS: To compare cardiorenal outcomes, mortality and safety between sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 inhibitors (SGLT-2i) and glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RA) in adults with Type 2 diabetes (T2D).
MATERIALS AND METHODS: We conducted a retrospective, new-user cohort study using the TriNetX global federated health research network. We identified 249 237 propensity score-matched pairs (498 474 total patients) who initiated SGLT-2i or GLP-1 RA between 2018 and 2023. The primary outcome was a kidney failure/death composite, defined as kidney failure, dialysis, kidney transplantation or all-cause mortality. Secondary outcomes included composite cardiovascular events, mortality and safety profiles.
RESULTS: SGLT-2i initiation was associated with a lower risk of the kidney failure/death composite compared with GLP-1 RA (HR: 0.87, 95% CI: 0.85-0.89). For the kidney-specific component, SGLT-2i initiation was associated with a lower risk of kidney failure, dialysis or kidney transplantation (HR: 0.74, 95% CI: 0.71-0.78), while all-cause mortality was also lower (HR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.88-0.93). The composite cardiovascular outcome (myocardial infarction, stroke, acute heart failure, cardiogenic shock, cardiac arrest or death) was broadly comparable between groups (HR: 0.98, 95% CI: 0.97-1.00).
CONCLUSIONS: SGLT-2i initiation was associated with lower risks of kidney failure-related outcomes and all-cause mortality compared with GLP-1 RA initiation, while cardiovascular outcomes were broadly comparable. These findings may inform individualized treatment selection in adults with T2D.
title: Real-World Comparison of Cardiorenal Outcomes With SGLT-2 Inhibitors Versus GLP-1 Receptor Agonists in Type 2 Diabetes.

abstract: Objective:To analyze the clinical efficacy of drug stent placement after resection of frontal sinus orbital communication lesions. Methods:Forty-six patients who underwent frontal sinus orbital communication lesion resection surgery in the hospital from January 2021 to December 2024 were selected and randomly divided into an observation group and a control group using a random number table method, with 23 patients in each group. The control group received routine treatment after surgery, while the observation group placed a fully degradable sinus drug stent in the surgical area on the basis of the control group. Compare the patency rate of frontal sinus drainage, classical Lund Kennedy（c-LK） score, modified olfactory fissure Lund Kennedy（oc-LK） score, and Lund Mackay CT score between two groups of patients at 30 and 90 days after surgery, and calculate the postoperative intervention rate and incidence of adverse reactions. Results:At 30 and 90 days after surgery, the frontal sinus drainage patency rates in the observation group were 95.65% and 86.96%, respectively, which were significantly higher than the control group's 52.17% and 43.48%（P<0.05）; The c-LK score, oc LK score, and Lund Mackay CT score of the observation group were significantly lower than those of the control group（P<0.05）; At 30 and 90 days after surgery, the intervention rate in the observation group was 8.70%, which was lower than the control group's 43.48% and 47.83%（P<0.05）; There was no statistically significant difference in the incidence of adverse reactions between the two groups（8.70% vs 4.35%）（P>0.05）. Conclusion:Implantation of fully degradable sinus drug stent after resection of frontal sinus orbital communication lesions can effectively maintain smooth drainage of the frontal sinus, reduce inflammation in the surgical area, lower the rate of postoperative re intervention, and effectively improve surgical efficacy. For patients with extensive lesion areas, severe intraoperative sinus mucosal damage, or high-risk factors for restenosis such as eosinophilic inflammation, the benefits are more definitive.

abstract: Fixed obstruction at the aortic isthmus may preclude transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Covered-stent implantation can restore large-bore access, but immediate passage of balloons and delivery systems through a newly implanted stent may expose it to longitudinal traction. Secondary stent migration during withdrawal of a valvuloplasty balloon and its intraluminal balloon-assisted rescue have not been well characterized. An 87-year-old man with New York Heart Association class III symptoms had severe bicuspid aortic stenosis (peak velocity, 4.4 m/s; mean gradient, 48 mmHg; valve area, 0.65 cm2; left ventricular ejection fraction, 55%) and a focal juxtaductal aortic-isthmus stenosis with a peak-to-peak gradient of 32 mmHg. Because of high surgical risk and unfavorable alternative access, same-session covered-stent treatment followed by transfemoral TAVR was selected. A 12 × 29-mm Advanta V12 covered stent was deployed and flared using an 18-mm noncompliant balloon. After aortic-valve predilation with a 23-mm noncompliant balloon, the stent migrated distally during balloon withdrawal. Guidewire access was preserved, and the stent remained coaxial. The balloon was recentered within the migrated stent and partially reinflated, allowing the balloon and stent to be advanced proximally as a single unit. After restoration and re-expansion of the stent, a 23-mm Myval valve was implanted successfully. Final transvalvular and isthmic gradients were 8 and 5 mmHg, respectively, with trivial paravalvular regurgitation and no aortic injury. The patient was discharged on day 3 and remained in NYHA class I at 6 months. Withdrawal of a large valvuloplasty balloon may cause secondary migration of a newly implanted aortic-isthmus stent. When guidewire access, coaxial alignment, and structural integrity are preserved, controlled intraluminal balloon-assisted repositioning may provide an effective bailout while maintaining transfemoral access.
journal: Catheterization and cardiovascular interventions : official journal of the Society for Cardiac Angiography & Interventions
title: Covered-Stent Migration During Same-Session Aortic Isthmus Repair and Bicuspid Aortic Valve TAVR.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery disease frequently coexists in patients undergoing transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), yet the benefit of routine percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) before TAVR remains uncertain.
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the efficacy and safety of routine PCI before TAVR compared with conservative or deferred revascularization.
METHODS: We pooled randomized clinical trials comparing PCI before TAVR versus no/deferred PCI in patients with concomitant coronary artery disease. Random-effects models estimated pooled relative risks (RRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Bayesian sensitivity analyses and trial sequential analysis were performed.
RESULTS: Three trials included 1156 patients (PCI, n = 579; no/deferred PCI, n = 577). In comparator arms reporting postrandomization PCI/revascularization, 72 of 461 patients (15.6%) underwent subsequent PCI/revascularization. PCI did not significantly reduce major adverse cardiac events (RR: 0.91, 95% CI: 0.70-1.18; I2 = 36.9%), myocardial infarction (RR: 0.86, 95% CI: 0.45-1.63; I2 = 49.8%), all-cause death (RR: 0.90, 95% CI: 0.70-1.15; I2 = 0.0%), or stroke (RR: 0.70, 95% CI: 0.48-1.03; P = 0.069; I2 = 0.0%). In two trials, PCI reduced urgent revascularization (RR: 0.33, 95% CI: 0.13-0.87; I2 = 54.5%) but increased major bleeding (RR: 1.57, 95% CI: 1.07-2.32; I2 = 37.9%) and any bleeding (RR: 1.77, 95% CI: 1.27-2.47; I2 = 66.7%). Bayesian analyses were directionally concordant. Trial sequential analysis was inconclusive for all efficacy outcomes.
CONCLUSION: Routine PCI before TAVR reduced urgent revascularization but increased bleeding, without significant differences in other outcomes. Current evidence remains underpowered to rule out benefit for other ischemic outcomes; larger trials are needed.

title: Percutaneous coronary intervention or medical therapy alone before transcatheter aortic valve replacement: insights from a meta-analysis of randomized trials.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Heart failure (HF) after acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains a major cause of morbidity and mortality despite advances in conventional therapy. Qili Qiangxin Capsule (QLQX) has been widely used as an adjunctive treatment for HF in China, but its efficacy and safety in patients with HF after AMI require further evaluation.
METHODS: Seven databases were searched from their inception to January 2026. Randomised controlled trials (RCTs) comparing QLQX plus conventional Western medicine (WM) with WM alone were included. The primary outcome was N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide (NT-proBNP). Secondary outcomes included left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF), B-type natriuretic peptide (BNP), left ventricular end-diastolic diameter (LVEDD), left ventricular end-systolic diameter (LVESD), left ventricular end-diastolic volume (LVEDV), clinical response rate, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein (hs-CRP), quality of life, all-cause mortality, heart failure-related hospitalisation, and adverse events. Meta-analysis was performed using RevMan 5.4.
RESULTS: A total of 16 RCTs involving 1391 participants were included. Compared with WM alone, QLQX plus WM was associated with greater reductions in NT-proBNP, BNP, LVEDD, LVESD, and hs-CRP, and improving LVEF, quality of life and the clinical response rate. No statistical differences were observed in LVEDV, all-cause mortality, and adverse events. Heart failure-related hospitalisation was not reported in any included study. The certainty of evidence for all outcomes was rated as low or very low according to the GRADE approach.
CONCLUSION: QLQX plus conventional WM was associated with improvements in several surrogate and short-term clinical outcomes in patients with HF after AMI. However, the certainty of evidence was low or very low, and data on mortality and heart failure-related hospitalisation were insufficient. The current evidence is therefore inadequate to determine whether QLQX improves long-term clinical prognosis. Further high-quality RCTs with longer follow-up and clinically important endpoints are needed.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420261277047, identifier CRD420261277047.
title: Qili Qiangxin capsule as adjunctive therapy for heart failure after acute myocardial infarction: a GRADE-assessed systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials.

abstract: Acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI) is uncommon in very young adults and may initially present with atypical symptoms, resulting in delayed recognition. Severe complications, such as cardiogenic shock and advanced conduction disturbances, can still occur despite limited conventional cardiovascular risk factors. A 21-year-old man initially presented with epigastric pain and was treated for a presumed gastrointestinal disorder. Further evaluation with electrocardiography later revealed acute anterior STEMI. On admission, he was hypotensive and bradycardic, with cardiogenic shock, complete atrioventricular block (CAVB), and right bundle branch block (RBBB). Coronary angiography demonstrated total occlusion of the left anterior descending artery. A PACE 101 H temporary transvenous pacemaker (Osypka Medical, Berlin, Germany) was inserted before primary percutaneous coronary intervention. Revascularisation using a GuReater CoCr Sirolimus-eluting Coronary Stent System (Lepu Medical Technology (Beijing) Co., Ltd., Beijing, China) successfully restored TIMI grade 3 flow. Following reperfusion, hemodynamic status and atrioventricular conduction improved rapidly, allowing pacemaker removal without permanent pacing. This case shows that extensive anterior STEMI can still occur in very young adults despite limited conventional cardiovascular risk factors. Delayed diagnosis may lead to severe complications, including cardiogenic shock and CAVB. However, timely reperfusion may allow recovery of ischemia-related conduction disturbances without permanent pacemaker implantation.
title: Acute Anterior ST-Elevation Myocardial Infarction With Right Bundle Branch Block Complicated by Complete Atrioventricular Block and Cardiogenic Shock in a 21-Year-Old Man: A Case Report.

abstract: Background Acute myocardial infarction is associated with significant morbidity and mortality, particularly due to ventricular arrhythmias and sudden cardiac death. QT dispersion (QTd), reflecting heterogeneity of ventricular repolarization, may provide useful information regarding ventricular electrical instability in patients with acute myocardial infarction. This study assessed QT dispersion and evaluated its association with clinical characteristics, ventricular arrhythmias, and in-hospital outcome. Methodology This prospective observational study was conducted in a tertiary care hospital from June 2025 to June 2026. A total of 100 patients diagnosed with acute myocardial infarction were enrolled after obtaining written informed consent and Institutional Ethics Committee approval. A standard 12-lead electrocardiogram (ECG) was recorded at presentation, and QTd was calculated as the difference between the maximum and minimum QT intervals. A QTd value >42 ms was considered abnormal. Associations between QTd and clinical characteristics, ventricular arrhythmias, and in-hospital outcome were evaluated using chi-square and independent-samples t-tests, as appropriate. Results The study included 100 patients. The mean QTd was 80.71 ± 18.2 ms, with QTd >42 ms observed in 88 (88.0%) patients. Ventricular arrhythmias occurred in 30 (30.0%) patients, and mean QTd was significantly higher among patients with ventricular arrhythmias than among those without (94.9 ± 17.5 vs. 70.4 ± 9.82 ms; p < 0.001). Ventricular premature contractions were observed in 20 (20.0%) patients, while ventricular tachycardia and ventricular fibrillation occurred in 5 (5.0%) patients each. Patients who died during hospitalization had significantly higher mean QTd than survivors (121.0 ± 22.0 vs. 70.64 ± 9.82 ms; p < 0.001). Conclusions Increased QTd was frequently observed in patients with acute myocardial infarction and was significantly associated with ventricular arrhythmias and in-hospital mortality. These findings represent associations and should not be interpreted as evidence of independent prognostic prediction or causality. Larger multicenter studies with standardized ECG assessment and appropriate adjustment for potential confounders are warranted to determine the independent prognostic significance of QTd in acute myocardial infarction.
title: Assessment of QT Dispersion in Patients With Acute Myocardial Infarction.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Globally, acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is the foremost cause of cardiovascular fatality, with dysregulated immune-inflammatory cascades serving as master regulators of both acute cardiomyocyte necrosis and subsequent maladaptive remodeling. Despite the prognostic potential of individual immune biomarkers, no multi-omics machine learning (ML)-derived immune gene signature has been established for predicting AMI outcome.
METHODS: Peripheral blood transcriptomes from four Gene Expression Omnibus datasets (GSE59867 as the discovery cohort; GSE48060, GSE60993, and GSE66360 as independent validation cohorts; total 348 participants) were subjected to study-wise differential expression analysis and marker-based immune scoring without cross-platform batch harmonization. Weighted gene co-expression network analysis (WGCNA) and nested machine learning (L2-regularized logistic regression, linear support vector machine (SVM), random forest, and gradient boosting) were used to derive an eight-gene diagnostic index. Signature performance was evaluated in three independent validation cohorts, contextualized at the single-cell resolution (GSE121893), and experimentally supported by in vitro reverse transcription quantitative polymerase chain reaction (RT-qPCR) using American Type Culture Collection (ATCC)-authenticated cell lines (THP-1 TIB-202 and EA.hy926 CRL-2922).
RESULTS: AMI specimens showed marked enrichment of pro-inflammatory M1-like macrophages, neutrophils, and exhausted CD8+ T cells compared to healthy donors. The WGCNA turquoise module exhibited the strongest phenotypic correlation (r = 0.78, p < 0.001). Convergent machine learning analysis yielded an eight-gene diagnostic index (BAX, EDA2R, MCEMP1, SOCS3, ASGR2, RNASE1, ADM, and KPNA5) with a repeated out-of-fold area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.984 in the discovery cohort and independent validation AUCs of 0.863, 0.655, and 0.876. Two exploratory binary-outcome analyses (6-month heart failure progression and 18-month recurrent events) yielded AUCs of 0.819 and 0.569, respectively; these small-sample results are descriptive only and do not support Kaplan-Meier or hazard ratio claims. In vitro RT-qPCR in ATCC-authenticated THP-1-derived macrophages (lipopolysaccharide/ATP stimulation) and EA.hy926 cells (hypoxia/reoxygenation) confirmed elevated levels of CXCL10 (3.82 ± 0.31-fold), IL6 (4.15 ± 0.44-fold), NLRP3 (2.94 ± 0.28-fold), and CASP1 (3.47 ± 0.38-fold) under AMI-relevant stimulation conditions (n = 3 independent biological replicates).
CONCLUSIONS: An eight-gene diagnostic index (BAX, EDA2R, MCEMP1, SOCS3, ASGR2, RNASE1, ADM, and KPNA5), derived using nested machine learning and validated in three independent cohorts, achieved robust discriminative accuracy for AMI diagnosis. Elevated inflammatory transcripts (CXCL10, IL6, NLRP3, and CASP1) confirmed by in vitro RT-qPCR in ATCC cell lines reflect concurrent inflammasome activation and immune dysregulation, offering a mechanistic rationale for precision immune-targeted intervention strategies.
title: Cross-cohort blood transcriptome analysis identifies an eight-gene diagnostic index and inflammatory programs in acute myocardial infarction.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Smart wrist-worn devices are increasingly used by patients after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) to monitor heart rate, rhythm-related alerts, sleep, activity, and other health-related data. However, limited qualitative evidence exists on how post-PCI patients interpret and respond to such information in daily life.
OBJECTIVE: This study aimed to explore how patients with coronary heart disease after PCI understand, evaluate, and respond to heart rate, heart rhythm, and health-related information generated by smart wrist-worn devices.
METHODS: A qualitative descriptive design was adopted. From January to May 2026, purposive sampling was used to recruit 23 post-PCI patients who had used smartwatches or smart bands in daily life. Semi-structured interviews were conducted, audio-recorded, transcribed verbatim, and analyzed using thematic analysis. Data collection and analysis were conducted concurrently until data saturation was achieved.
RESULTS: Four themes were developed: (1) cardiac status became continuously datafied; (2) calibrating risk between alerts and sensations; (3) device information awaited medical interpretation; and (4) from self-management to disease burden. Patients did not simply accept or reject device-generated data. Instead, they interpreted alerts by comparing them with bodily sensations, previous cardiac events, stent implantation experiences, follow-up results, and healthcare professionals' explanations. Device information could enhance awareness of medication use, follow-up, and lifestyle management. However, when alerts lacked medical interpretation or follow-up response, they also increased uncertainty, worry, repeated self-monitoring, and perceived disease burden.
CONCLUSIONS: Smart wrist-worn devices may support daily observation and clinician-patient communication in post-PCI management, but they should not be regarded as substitutes for clinical examinations or professional judgment. Clearer interpretive boundaries, stratified guidance, and follow-up response pathways are needed to help patients appropriately understand and act on device-generated information.
title: Between algorithmic alerts and bodily sensations: a qualitative study of post-PCI patients' experiences with wrist-worn heart health information.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Pulmonary embolism (PE) is a leading cause of cardiovascular death, with prior studies suggesting differences in clinical characteristics and risk factors between males and females.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed all 1,000 adult patients with confirmed PE evaluated by the Pulmonary Embolism Response Team (PERT) at Corewell Health West from November 2019 to March 2024 to describe sex-based differences in presentation, management, and outcomes. Based on sex, patients were classified by differences in demographic, clinical, biomarker, treatment, and outcome measures, including 30-day and one-year survival.
RESULTS: Among 1,000 patients, 480 (48%) were female. Females were older (64 vs. 62.4 years; p = 0.028), had higher body mass index (35.5 vs. 32.2; p < 0.001), and more frequently reported hormone use (21% vs. 5%; p < 0.001). Troponin and Pro-BNP elevations were higher in proportion in females, while males were more likely to smoke (26% vs. 15%; p < 0.001) and present with cough (31% vs. 23%; p = 0.005). No significant sex differences were observed in PE severity, catheter-based interventions, inferior vena cava filter placement, or 30-day (females 8.7%, males 5.8%; p = 0.064) and one-year survival (females 85.4%, males 87.9%; p = 0.217).
CONCLUSION: Despite differences in baseline characteristics and certain clinical features, PE severity, interventions, and outcomes were similar between sexes in this PERT-managed cohort. This highlights sex-specific variations in presentation without differences in management or outcomes within a standardized multidisciplinary pathway such as PERT.
title: Sex-Based Differences in Clinical Characteristics and Outcomes in Patients with Acute Pulmonary Embolism. An Analysis of 1000 Pulmonary Embolism Response Team Activations.
