Antithrombotic Treatment After PCI in Older Patients With Atrial Fibrillation: Navigating Bleeding, Mortality, and Clinical Complexity.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Recent clinical trials have demonstrated that clopidogrel monotherapy is superior to aspirin for long-term maintenance after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, evidence remains limited regarding whether the clinical benefit of chronic clopidogrel monotherapy differs according to CYP2C19 genotype.
OBJECTIVES: The study sought to investigate the prognostic impact of CYP2C19 genotype in patients with clopidogrel monotherapy for long-term maintenance following PCI.
METHODS: From the SMART-CHOICE 3 (SMart Angioplasty Research Team: CHoice of Optimal Anti-Thrombotic Strategy in Patients Undergoing Implantation of Coronary Drug-Eluting Stents 3) trial and the nationwide PTRG-DES (Platelet Function and genoType-Related Long-term progGosis in DES-treated Patients) consortium, we analyzed patients with CYP2C19 genotyping who completed the standard duration of dual antiplatelet therapy after PCI without cardiovascular events. Patients were classified according to CYP2C19 loss-of-function allele status: rapid or normal metabolizer vs intermediate or poor metabolizer (IM/PM). The primary outcome was a composite of all-cause death, myocardial infarction, and stroke at 3 years after switching to clopidogrel monotherapy.
RESULTS: Of 1,352 patients, 807 patients were carriers of a loss-of-function allele (IM/PM). The risk of primary outcome did not differ between the IM/PM and rapid or normal metabolizer groups (1.2% vs 2.2%; adjusted HR: 0.53; 95% CI: 0.20-1.44; P = 0.215). Likewise, the risk of major bleeding was comparable between the groups (1.1% vs 2.0%; adjusted HR: 0.40; 95% CI: 0.14-1.14; P = 0.086). Subgroup analyses consistently showed no significant interaction between CYP2C19 genotype and primary outcome.
CONCLUSIONS: In patients who completed the standard duration of dual antiplatelet therapy following PCI, clinical effects of clopidogrel monotherapy were consistent across CYP2C19 genotypes. These findings provide clinical reassurance that clopidogrel monotherapy can be used effectively for long-term maintenance, regardless of CYP2C19 genotype. (SMart Angioplasty Research Team: CHoice of Optimal Anti-Thrombotic Strategy in Patients Undergoing Implantation of Coronary Drug-Eluting Stents 3 [SMART-CHOICE 3]; NCT04418479; Platelet Function and genoType-Related Long-term progGosis in DES-treated Patients [PTRG-DES]; NCT04734028).
keywords: major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events
title: Prognostic Implication of CYP2C19 Genotype During Chronic Clopidogrel Monotherapy After Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) counterpulsation raises aortic diastolic pressure every cycle (1:1) or alternate cycles (1:2, weaning). Whether they reach peripheral photoplethysmography (PPG) is unknown; 1 report described 1:1 only.
CASE SUMMARY: An 82-year-old man in IABP-supported cardiogenic shock had finger and thenar PPG on 1:1, 1:2, removal, and twice afterward. An augmented diastolic peak appeared on every finger beat on 1:1 and alternate beats on 1:2, barring ectopy, and none afterward. Perfusion index reached a nadir at removal and rose through recovery; finger-thenar coherence followed a similar trend.
DISCUSSION: Peripheral PPG encoded assist ratio and weaning state. The augmented peak was proportionally larger at the finger than in the aorta, raising the hypothesis that it reflects root- and arch-supplied territories.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Ordinary peripheral PPG carries a beat-resolved signature of IABP counterpulsation and of the weaning course, without vascular access.
title: Multisite Peripheral Photoplethysmography Captures Intra-Aortic Balloon Pump Counterpulsation and Weaning State in Cardiogenic Shock.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Fluid overload-associated large B-cell lymphoma (FO-LBCL) is a rare malignancy presenting with serous effusions without solid masses.
CASE SUMMARY: We report an 83-year-old man developing substantial pericardial effusion 19 months post-left atrial appendage closure. Although a device-related complication was initially suspected, pericardial fluid analysis and fluorine-18 fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography established a definitive diagnosis of FO-LBCL. Because of severe cardiovascular comorbidities and anthracycline cardiotoxicity risks, standard rituximab, cyclophosphamide, doxorubicin, vincristine, and prednisone was contraindicated. Instead, an individualized, anthracycline-free regimen with 3 cycles of rituximab monotherapy followed by 3 cycles of rituximab, cyclophosphamide, vincristine, and prednisolone cycles was administered. The patient achieved remission and remained recurrence-free during 18-month follow-up.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: The present case highlights the critical need to exclude malignancies in post-left atrial appendage closure effusions and demonstrates the efficacy of attenuated, anthracycline-free chemoimmunotherapy for elderly patients with FO-LBCL high cardiovascular risk.
title: Pericardial Effusion Revealing Fluid Overload-Associated Large B-Cell Lymphoma After Left Atrial Appendage Closure.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage (aSAH) is complicated by Takotsubo syndrome (TTS) in 15% to 25% of patients. Managed with supportive care, TTS with refractory cardiogenic shock represents a challenging complication with limited published guidance.
CASE SUMMARY: A 78-year-old woman presented with high-grade aSAH requiring external ventricular drain placement, stent-assisted aneurysm coiling, and dual antiplatelet therapy complicated by TTS and cardiogenic shock refractory to pressors and inotropes. A microaxial flow pump (Impella 5.5) was deployed, with full myocardial and neurological recovery.
DISCUSSION: Often self-limiting but causing secondary injury, TTS secondary to neurologic injury is driven by catecholamine-mediated myocardial injury. Mechanical circulatory support has been reported for TTS and refractory cardiogenic shock. After conducting a literature review, we believe this is the first reported use of an Impella 5.5 for refractory cardiogenic shock from TTS secondary to subarachnoid hemorrhage.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: Microaxial flow pump rescue appears to be a viable strategy for refractory cardiogenic shock complicating high-grade aSAH, even during dual-antiplatelet therapy.
title: High-Grade Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage Complicated by Refractory Cardiogenic Shock Successfully Treated With Microaxial Flow Pump.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) is an approved treatment option for select high-risk patients with symptomatic mitral regurgitation (MR). The main cohort of the ENCIRCLE trial, evaluating fully percutaneous transseptal TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system, demonstrated 13.9% mortality, significant MR reduction, and improved functional and health status outcomes at 1 year.
OBJECTIVES: We report 2-year outcomes from the main cohort of the ENCIRCLE trial.
METHODS: Eligible symptomatic patients with ≥3+ MR who were not suitable for surgery or transcatheter edge-to-edge repair underwent TMVR with the SAPIEN M3 system. Independent study oversight included an echocardiographic core laboratory and a clinical events committee. Endpoints included the nonhierarchical composite rate of all-cause mortality or heart failure hospitalization (HFH) as well as clinical, echocardiographic, functional, and health status outcomes.
RESULTS: A total of 299 patients were treated, with 2-year follow-up data available for 202 of 210 eligible patients (96.2%). Mean age was 75.5 ± 9.3 years, 50.8% were men, and the mean Society of Thoracic Surgeons Predicted Risk of Mortality score for mitral valve replacement was 6.6% ± 4.1%. At 2 years, MR reduction was sustained, with MR ≤1+ in 97.0% patients (P < 0.001). The 2-year composite rate of all-cause mortality or HFH was 35.6% (25.1% all-cause mortality, 23.0% HFH). In a 365-day landmark analysis, 1- to 2-year rates were 13.0% for all-cause mortality and 10.6% for first HFH. At 2 years, the rates of disabling stroke, clinically significant valve thrombosis, and hemolysis requiring intervention were 6.6%, 7.1%, and 7.6%, respectively. There were no instances of clinically significant left ventricular outflow obstruction. Improvements in functional and health status outcomes were sustained with 87.0% of patients in NYHA functional class I/II (P < 0.001) and a mean Kansas City Cardiomyopathy Questionnaire overall summary score increase of 17.2 points (P < 0.001). The 6-minute walk distance increased by +9.0 ± 97.3 m compared to baseline (P = 0.246).
CONCLUSIONS: The 2-year results of the ENCIRCLE trial demonstrated durable near MR elimination with sustained improvements in functional and health status outcomes in surviving patients. These findings support transseptal TMVR as a therapeutic option for carefully selected patients with symptomatic MR. (The ENCIRCLE Trial [ENCIRCLE]; NCT04153292).
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
title: Percutaneous Transcatheter Mitral Valve Replacement for Symptomatic Mitral Regurgitation: 2-Year Outcomes From the ENCIRCLE Trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite advances in transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR), access-site vascular complications remain an important source of procedural morbidity. The conventional double-ProGlide strategy may increase the risk of access-site stenosis and other vascular complications, particularly in patients with challenging iliofemoral anatomy. Retrospective studies have suggested that a single-ProGlide strategy may offer an effective alternative, but this strategy has not yet been evaluated in a randomized trial.
OBJECTIVES: This trial aimed to determine whether a single-ProGlide strategy could offer a simpler alternative to the conventional double-ProGlide strategy without increasing vascular complications.
METHODS: The SINGLE-CLOSURE trial was a prospective, multicenter, open-label, randomized trial conducted at 25 centers in China. Patients aged ≥65 years scheduled for transfemoral TAVR were assigned 1:1 to single-ProGlide or double-ProGlide closure for the main access site. The primary endpoint was the in-hospital composite of Valve Academic Research Consortium (VARC)-3-defined access-site or access-related major and minor vascular complications.
RESULTS: A total of 876 patients were randomized. In the modified intention-to-treat population, the primary endpoint occurred in 57 of 436 patients (13.1%) in the single-ProGlide group and 65 of 430 patients (15.1%) in the double-ProGlide group, meeting the prespecified criterion for noninferiority (risk difference: -2.2%; 95%: -7.0% to 2.6%; P = 0.013; noninferiority margin: 3.19%). Access-related major vascular complications occurred in 2 patients (0.5%) in the single-ProGlide group and 6 patients (1.4%) in the double-ProGlide group. Among the secondary endpoints, individual components of the primary endpoint, access-related bleeding, time to hemostasis, and all-cause mortality were similar between groups. Access-site stenosis was numerically less frequent with the single-ProGlide strategy (5.0% vs 7.9%), whereas additional closure devices might be used more often (2.5% vs 0.9%).
CONCLUSIONS: A single-ProGlide strategy was noninferior to conventional double-ProGlide closure for the composite of VARC-3-defined access-site or access-related vascular complications after transfemoral TAVR. Primary endpoint events were predominantly minor vascular complications.
journal: Journal of the American College of Cardiology
title: Single vs Double ProGlide Devices for Access Site Closure after Transfemoral Aortic Valve Replacement: The SINGLE-CLOSURE Trial.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: Ticagrelor is an oral reversible platelet P2Y12 inhibitor that improves ischaemic outcomes in atherosclerotic cardiovascular disease, including the prevention of stent thrombosis after percutaneous coronary intervention, at the cost of increased bleeding risk.
AREAS COVERED: A comprehensive literature search was performed across PubMed and Web of Science (inception to January 2026). This case-based review outlines the current guidance surrounding bleeding events and emergent surgery on oral P2Y12 inhibitors, treatment options for reversing their effects, and describes a novel ticagrelor reversal agent in two cases of life-threatening bleeding, one related to gastrointestinal haemorrhage and one associated with emergent coronary artery bypass graft surgery.
EXPERT OPINION: Ticagrelor is a first-line treatment for acute coronary syndromes but is associated with heightened bleeding risk, especially when combined with aspirin. Ticagrelor's reversibility may offer advantages over the irreversibly-acting thienopyridine P2Y12 inhibitors. Patients treated with potent antiplatelet regimens may require rapid and effective restoration of haemostatic activity in addition to supportive measures in those presenting with life-threatening haemorrhage or requiring emergent surgery. We summarise the current available treatment options to reverse antiplatelet activity and highlight the role of ticagrelor reversal with bentracimab in improving haemostasis in emergency settings.
title: Reversing ticagrelor P2Y12 inhibition in life-threatening haemorrhage: a case-based review.

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: Mitral regurgitation (MR) is commonly treated with ring-based annuloplasty. In case of recurrent MR, re-do operations are often denied due to high risk. Transcatheter valve-in-ring (V-i-R) procedures offer an alternative. This study assessed the feasibility and outcomes of using the transapical, repositionable Tendyne valve for off-label mitral V-i-R procedures, as an alternative to balloon-expandable valves like SAPIEN, which face limitations such as paravalvular leakage and LVOT obstruction.
METHODS: The TEND-RING registry is a retrospective, international study with prospective follow-up, including 16 high-risk patients from eight European centers who underwent Tendyne V-i-R procedures between 2017 and 2024. Procedural, 30-day, and long-term outcomes were analyzed.
RESULTS: Patients were elderly (median age 79.5), predominantly male (81%), with significant comorbidities (STS Risk of Mortality 5.6%, 4.4-7.2%) and severe MR (3 + /4 +). Procedural success was 100%, with no LVOT obstruction or device embolization. MR was reduced to mild or none in all patients. 30-day mortality was 6.3%. Over a median 11-month follow-up, five deaths occurred (31.3%), three from cardiovascular causes (18.75%). Surviving patients showed sustained MR reduction and improved symptoms (89% in NYHA I/II). Ring size analysis suggested a minimum of 36 mm for rigid/semi-rigid rings, while flexible bands allowed successful implantation in sizes as small as 30 mm.
CONCLUSIONS: Tendyne V-i-R procedures are technically feasible, effective, and safe in selected high-risk patients with recurrent MR. Ring size thresholds identified may guide patient selection and procedural planning in future interventions.
journal: Clinical research in cardiology : official journal of the German Cardiac Society
title: Transapical mitral valve-in-ring implantation: Results of the real-world European Tendyne valve-in-ring registry.

abstract: Circulating cell-free DNA (cfDNA) has emerged as a potential biomarker for cardiovascular injury, yet its clinical relevance in acute myocardial infarction (AMI) remains underexplored. cfDNA from 107 AMI patients and 32 healthy controls were isolated and its associations with clinical, demographic and biochemical profiling were explored. Patients were stratified by chest pain duration (0-24 h) to assess cross-sectional temporal trends. cfDNA levels showed six-fold elevation in AMI patients compared to controls and were associated with adverse cardiometabolic and lifestyle risk factors. cfDNA levels increased progressively with chest pain duration, peaking for 18-24 h (median:55.31 ng/mL), and strongly correlated with hs-cTnT (rho = 0.535) and NT-proBNP (rho = 0.615) during this phase. Overall diagnostic performance of cfDNA was good (AUC = 0.858), which further improved in late-phase AMI (AUC = 0.904). Strong diagnostic performance of cfDNA, particularly in the late phase AMI, suggests its potential as a complementary tool to existing cardiac biomarkers.
title: Evaluating the Cross-sectional Temporal Trends, Diagnostic and Clinical Relevance of Cell Free DNA in Acute Myocardial Infarction.

abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) has profoundly changed the management of severe aortic stenosis (AS), evolving from a treatment reserved for inoperable and high-risk patients to an established therapeutic option across a wide surgical risk spectrum. Although the expansion of TAVI indications has been largely supported by randomized clinical trials conducted in high-income countries, real-world experience and technological contributions from distinct healthcare systems are increasingly relevant. Brazil has played a significant role in the early adoption, structured implementation, and clinical evaluation of TAVI in Latin America. Since the first procedures performed in 2008, Brazilian centers have developed Heart Team models, contributed to national and regional registries, and generated real-world evidence demonstrating procedural safety and effectiveness comparable to international benchmarks, despite the presence of resource limitations and a higher prevalence of complex clinical and anatomical scenarios. The incorporation of TAVI into the Brazilian public health system in 2022 marked a major milestone in expanding access to minimally invasive therapy for patients with severe AS. In parallel, Brazilian scientific societies have adapted international guideline recommendations to local practice, supporting evidence-based patient selection across different surgical risk categories. Notably, Brazil has also emerged as a developer of locally engineered transcatheter valve technologies, highlighting its transition from a technology consumer to an active contributor in the field of structural heart disease. This review summarizes the historical evolution, national experience, clinical outcomes, guideline integration, technological innovation, and health economic considerations of TAVI in Brazil.
title: State of Art of Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation for the Treatment of Aortic Stenosis in Low-Risk Patients: A Perspective on Brazilian Contributions and Implementation Challenges.

abstract: Chronic inflammatory vascular diseases are increasingly recognized as systemic disorders sustained by maladaptive cross-organ immunometabolic coupling, yet current therapeutic strategies remain largely lesion-centered and fail to address upstream drivers of disease persistence. Here, we identify the gut-immune-vascular axis as a system-level pathogenic unit that integrates gut microbial dysbiosis, intestinal barrier dysfunction, metabolic imbalance, and vascular immune activation into a self-reinforcing pathological circuit. Through integrated clinical profiling and cross-species validation, we demonstrate that disruption of this axis is characterized by coordinated probiotic depletion, expansion of proinflammatory taxa, translocation of microbial endotoxins, accumulation of microbiota-derived metabolites, and macrophage polarization toward a proinflammatory phenotype along the gut-vascular continuum. To therapeutically target this axis, we engineer enzyme-responsive synbiotic microspheres that codeliver probiotics, a microbial metabolic pathway inhibitor, and a prebiotic within a protective polymeric matrix, enabling site-specific intestinal activation and coordinated microbiota-metabolic modulation. This engineered system restores intestinal barrier integrity, reprograms microbial ecology and metabolite output, suppresses immunometabolic dysfunction, and robustly attenuates pathological vascular remodeling across cellular, murine, and large-animal models, with in-stent restenosis serving as a representative disease context. Collectively, this work establishes axis-oriented immunometabolic reprogramming as a generalizable therapeutic paradigm and highlights engineered synbiotic platforms as scalable tools for system-level intervention in chronic inflammatory diseases.
title: Engineered synbiotic microspheres enable system-level reprogramming of the gut-immune-vascular axis in chronic inflammatory vascular disease.

abstract:
RATIONALE: Coronary microvascular dysfunction may contribute to persistent angina after fractional flow reserve (FFR)-guided coronary management. Whether disclosure of the index of microcirculatory resistance (IMR) and personalized management improve angina-related health status remains unknown.
PRIMARY HYPOTHESIS: Among participants with initial IMR ≥25, disclosure of IMR with protocol-guided personalized management will improve the baseline-adjusted 12-month Seattle Angina Questionnaire (SAQ) Summary Score compared with concealed IMR and usual care.
DESIGN: DECISIONING is an investigator-initiated, 16-center French randomized trial (planned n=280). All participants have angina and at least one angiographic lesion ≥50%; FFR and initial IMR are measured before randomization. FFR ≤0.80 guides percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI), whereas PCI is deferred when FFR >0.80. Participants are randomized 1:1, stratified by center and initial IMR (<25 or ≥25), to IMR disclosure with individualized treatment or IMR-concealed usual care. Participants and treating clinicians are aware of allocation; the initial IMR value remains concealed from control participants and their treating clinicians. Centralized follow-up and outcome assessment are blinded. Coronary flow reserve (CFR) is collected for exploratory secondary physiologic characterization but does not guide randomization or treatment. Enrollment and status Enrollment began on March 31, 2022. As of September 19, 2026, 275 participants had been randomized; enrollment toward 280 was ongoing, with final follow-up expected in october 2028.
CONCLUSIONS: DECISIONING will test the clinical benefit of IMR-informed management while characterizing complementary CFR/IMR physiology in exploratory analyses. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov; NCT05178914; https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT05178914.
title: Index of microcirculatory resistance-guided management in angina: design and rationale of the DECISIONING trial.

abstract:
AIMS: Transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER) has emerged as an established therapeutic option for selected patients with severe mitral (MR) and tricuspid regurgitation (TR), supported by expanding clinical evidence. However, intraprocedural assessment of residual regurgitation remains challenging because of dynamic hemodynamic changes, device-related artefacts, and limitations of conventional echocardiographic parameters.
METHODS AND RESULTS: This review summarizes current evidence on multiparametric echocardiographic and hemodynamic assessment during mitral (M-TEER) and tricuspid (T-TEER) procedures, with a focus on the evaluation of residual regurgitation, the immediate physiological response, markers of cardiac remodeling and their prognostic implications. Accurate quantification of residual MR and TR requires an integrated multiparametric approach. Residual regurgitation is associated with clinical outcomes and reverse remodeling. Conventional two-dimensional measures are limited by altered post-procedural jet geometry and multiple residual jets. Three-dimensional vena contracta area provides improved visualization and quantification of residual regurgitation, enabling summation of multiple jets. However, its quantitative accuracy has been validated only to a limited extent and thresholds after TEER are not standardized. Volumetric quantification is independent of jet geometry but remains insufficiently validated intraprocedurally. Atrial pressures, venous flow and forward flow describe the physiological response rather than regurgitant severity.
CONCLUSION: Intraprocedural evaluation of residual MR and TR after TEER requires expert integration of multiple echocardiographic measures of regurgitation with complementary assessment of its physiological consequences and hemodynamic parameters. Advanced 3D imaging plays an increasingly central role in improving procedural assessment and post-interventional risk stratification, but standardized and validated criteria for quantifying residual regurgitation after TEER are still lacking.
authors: SIC (Italian Society of Cardiology) Echocardiography Study Group
title: Intraprocedural evaluation of residual mitral and tricuspid regurgitation after transcatheter edge-to-edge repair.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Patients with LVEF 36-50% and cardiac autonomic dysfunction remain at risk after myocardial infarction (MI) despite not qualifying for primary-preventive defibrillator therapy. Implantable cardiac monitor (ICM)-based telemonitoring facilitates early detection of serious arrhythmic events (SArE), however it remains unclear whether infarct type modifies the detection and prognostic significance of SArE.
OBJECTIVE: To compare the effect of ICM monitoring on SArE detection by infarct type and explore associations with subsequent major adverse cardiovascular and cerebrovascular events (MACCE).
METHODS: SMART-MI randomized MI survivors with LVEF 36-50% and cardiac autonomic dysfunction to ICM-based telemonitoring or conventional follow-up. Cox models assessed effects on SArE detection and treatment-by-infarct-type interaction. Exploratory analyses modeled detected SArE as a time-dependent covariate, stratified by arm, for subsequent MACCE.
RESULTS: 400 patients were randomized to ICM implantation (n=201, 122 STEMI) or conventional follow-up (n=199, 114 STEMI). Telemedical monitoring increased SArE detection in STEMI (HR 11.99, 95% CI 3.67-39.17) and NSTEMI (HR 4.44, 95% CI 2.09-9.43; both p<0.001). Although the effect was numerically greater in STEMI, clinically relevant effect modification cannot be excluded (p for interaction=0.154). Detected SArE were associated with subsequent MACCE in both, STEMI and NSTEMI with HR of 7.77 (95% CI 3.20-18.86) and 4.26 (95% CI 1.44-12.58), respectively.
CONCLUSION: ICM-based telemonitoring increased SArE detection in both STEMI and NSTEMI patients and detected SArE were associated with subsequent MACCE in both infarct types. These findings support further investigation of intensified rhythm-surveillance strategies in high-risk STEMI and NSTEMI patients.
title: Impact of Infarct Type on Serious Arrhythmic Event Detection and Cardiovascular Outcomes During Telemedical Monitoring After Myocardial Infarction: A SMART-MI substudy.

abstract: Contrast-associated acute kidney injury (CA-AKI) is a risk of percutaneous coronary interventions (PCI) for chronic total coronary occlusions (CTO), and complex interventional procedures in general. The incidence and temporal changes of CA-AKI with contemporary CTO techniques had not been evaluated before in a large registry. Therefore, we analyzed 12911 CTO procedures by 27 operators between 2015 and 2024 with pre and postprocedural serum creatinine (SCr) assessment. CA-AKI was defined as an increase in SCr ≥0.3 mg/dl or ≥50% from baseline SCr. In addition, an older definition was applied as CIN (Contrast induced nephropathy: SCr increase ≥0.5 mg/dl or ≥25% of baseline). The incidence of CA-AKI was 3.91% with a slight temporal decrease from 5.0% in 2015 to 3.7% in 2024. CIN was 5.96%, however, the operator-reported CIN was only 1.68%. The major determinants of CA-AKI were age, diabetes, peripheral disease, reduced ejection fraction, chronic kidney disease stage ≥2, and fluoroscopy time. The highest impact had the incidence of pericardial tamponade. Procedural perforations were more frequent in CA-AKI patients (10.3 vs 3.3%; p<0.001), and in-hospital mortality (0.9 vs 0.2%; p<0.001) was increased. Contrast volume (CV) was one of the determinants of CA-AKI. No CA-AKI occurred in procedures with <50ml, which was achieved in only 0.5%. In conclusion, CA-AKI remains a relevant procedural complication of CTO PCI even with modern techniques with a slight decrease during the past decade and reduced CV use. Pericardial tamponade had the strongest association with CA-AKI. Ultra-low contrast PCI may not be feasible in an all-comer cohort.
title: Contrast-Associated Acute Kidney Injury Following Recanalization Of Chronic Total Coronary Occlusions In A Large Multi-Center Registry.

abstract:
AIM OF STUDY: This review summarizes current evidence on MACE definitions, the timing and magnitude of post-ACS risk, its main drivers, and evidence-based risk-reduction strategies, and identifies key methodological gaps.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This narrative synthesis includes randomized controlled trials, meta-analyses, large registries, and observational studies reporting MACE after ACS, identified through PubMed and cross-referenced guideline documents. No systematic search protocol or quantitative synthesis was performed; priority was given to peer-reviewed publications, current guidelines, and high-impact meta-analyses, with sources cited for pooled estimates.
RESULTS: MACE definitions are heterogeneous. The classical 3-point composite (cardiovascular death, nonfatal myocardial infarction, nonfatal stroke) is the regulatory standard, but 4- and 5-point versions incorporating revascularization, unstable angina, or heart-failure hospitalization are common, and administrative datasets often substitute all-cause mortality. Broader definitions inflate event rates and can affect interpretation of treatment effects. Data from one of the largest meta-analyses indicate that nearly half of the adverse events during the first year occur within 90 days, with an overall 90-day MACE rate of 4.1%. However, it should be noted that one-year rates range from 3.6% in a small cohort of lower-risk patients to 34.4% in a large national registry, reflecting differences in patient composition, the completeness of revascularization performed, and definitions of MACE components. The strongest predictors of post-ACS MACE were clinical severity (Killip class >II, cardiogenic shock/arrest, LVEF ≤40%), comorbidity burden (chronic kidney disease, diabetes, hypertension, dyslipidemia, smoking, age/frailty), and anatomical/procedural factors (multivessel disease, incomplete revascularization, suboptimal TIMI flow). Complete revascularization, high-intensity statin therapy, individualized dual antiplatelet duration, and structured secondary prevention were each associated with reduced MACE.
CONCLUSIONS: Post-ACS MACE clusters within 90 days after discharge. However, reported incidence varies widely due to heterogeneous endpoint definitions and population differences. Standardizing MACE definition and adjudication reporting, and designing trials powered for early endpoints, would meaningfully improve evidence synthesis. Clinicians should prioritize complete revascularization, optimized lipid-lowering, individualized antithrombotic therapy, and early, intensive secondary prevention.
title: MAJOR ADVERSE CARDIOVASCULAR EVENTS AFTER ACUTE CORONARY SYNDROME: DEFINITION, TIMING, RATES, MAIN RISK FACTORS, AND WAYS TO IMPROVE.

abstract: Hypertension remains the leading modifiable risk factor for cardiovascular morbidity and mortality. However, rates of global blood pressure (BP) control remain suboptimal, despite effective pharmacologic therapies and clear guideline targets. Persistent gaps in control are multifactorial, including poor adherence, complex treatment regimens, and health care system limitations. Renal denervation (RDN), a device-based therapy, is an emerging treatment which may overcome barriers for hypertension control. RDN targets renal sympathetic nerve activity, a key contributor to hypertension pathophysiology. Early studies of RDN, using catheter-based ablation techniques, suggested substantial BP reductions (∼10-30 mmHg reduction in office systolic BP). However, initial enthusiasm was tempered by neutral findings in sham-controlled trials. Recent advances in device technology, procedural optimization, technique, and patient selection have been central to improving reproducibility and redemonstrating efficacy (office and ambulatory BP) and safety of RDN in contemporary randomized studies. Current evidence supports RDN as an adjunctive therapy in carefully selected patients with resistant or uncontrolled primary hypertension, particularly in those with preserved renal function and evidence of sympathetic overactivity. As the field evolves, ongoing research focusing on precision phenotyping, noncatheter-based techniques, long-term clinical outcomes, and cost-effectiveness will be critical in defining the role of RDN within contemporary hypertension management strategies.
journal: Advances in kidney disease and health
title: Renal Denervation in Modern Hypertension Care: From Early Promise to Evidence-Based Clinical Integration.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Platelet reactivity testing may help tailor antithrombotic regimens after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). We sought to describe antithrombotic practices and assess 30-day outcomes in patients treated at an academic cardiac catheterization laboratory who underwent platelet reactivity testing following PCI while concurrently on oral anticoagulation (AC).
METHODS: Patients on oral AC who underwent PCI and received platelet reactivity testing at an academic medical center between 1/2012 and 9/2022 were reviewed. Patients were grouped by high on-treatment platelet reactivity (PRU ≥208) and a low on-treatment platelet reactivity (PRU <208) status and then analyzed based on whether they were continued on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) or de-escalated to single antiplatelet therapy (SAPT). Rates of major bleeding and stent thrombosis up to 30 days post-PCI were compared using univariate and multivariate analyses.
RESULTS: 156 patients were included (mean age 74, 72% male). Post-PCI, platelet reactivity testing revealed adequate platelet inhibition (PRU < 208) in 120 patients (77%) and inadequate inhibition (PRU≥208) in 36 patients (23%). In the group with adequate inhibition, 78 patients (65%) were de-escalated to SAPT. Compared to individuals with adequate inhibition that were continued on DAPT, patients in the SAPT group had a lower rate of major bleeding 30 days post-PCI (1.3% vs. 9.5%, p = 0.05) and with no increase in stent thrombosis rates. In the group with inadequate inhibition, 53% of patients were de-escalated to SAPT, most often with an alternative P2Y12 inhibitor. Compared to individuals with inadequate inhibition that were continued on DAPT, these patients had lower rates of major bleeding at 30 days (0% vs. 12%, p = 0.23) and similar rates of stent thrombosis.
DISCUSSION: In this analysis of a high bleeding and ischemic risk cohort of patients on concurrent AC undergoing PCI at a high-volume academic medical center, patients managed with SAPT post-PCI experienced lower rates of bleeding without a clear increase in ischemic events compared to those continued on DAPT. Antiplatelet de-escalation was left to the treating physician's discretion, and larger prospective studies are needed to corroborate the safety and utility of this strategy in clinical practice.
journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
title: The use of platelet function testing to guide antithrombotic regimens post-percutaneous coronary intervention in patients requiring therapeutic anticoagulation.
The fifth universal definition of myocardial infarction (2026): A new revolution for our practice?

abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate the diagnostic performance of CT-derived fractional flow reserve (CT-FFR) for detecting haemodynamically significant coronary disease in patients with anatomically long-segment lesions.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: This retrospective multicentre study included patients who underwent coronary CT angiography and invasive pressure-wire FFR within 30 days. Anatomically long-segment disease was defined as lesion length ≥ 20 mm. Invasive FFR ≤ 0.80 was the reference standard. CT-FFR was assessed at vessel and patient levels, with patient-level CT-FFR defined as the minimum value per patient and patient-level disease as any invasive FFR ≤ 0.80. Diagnostic discrimination, threshold-based classification, and Bland-Altman agreement were evaluated.
RESULTS: The diagnostic cohort included 329 patients and 377 vessels; 137 patients and 144 vessels had anatomically long-segment disease. At the vessel level, CT-FFR achieved an AUC of 0.941 (95% CI: 0.917-0.966), sensitivity of 94.3%, specificity of 83.7%, and accuracy of 88.6%. In anatomically long-segment vessels, the AUC was 0.961 (95% CI: 0.922-1.000), with sensitivity of 95.7%, specificity of 92.2%, and accuracy of 94.4%. At the patient level, the overall AUC was 0.941 (95% CI: 0.915-0.967) and 0.971 (95% CI: 0.934-1.000) in anatomically long-segment disease. Mean bias was small, although limits of agreement were clinically relevant.
CONCLUSION: CT-FFR showed high diagnostic discrimination for invasive FFR-defined ischaemia, including in anatomically long-segment disease. However, agreement limits and threshold-zone uncertainty support its use as a non-invasive physiological adjunct rather than a direct substitute for invasive pressure-wire assessment.
KEY POINTS: Question Does machine learning-based CT-FFR maintain diagnostic performance for invasive FFR-defined ischaemia in anatomically long-segment coronary lesions? Findings CT-derived FFR showed high diagnostic discrimination overall and maintained performance in anatomically long-segment disease, although subgroup comparisons remained exploratory. Clinical relevance CT-derived FFR may provide non-invasive physiological information in anatomically long-segment coronary disease before invasive angiography, while values near the 0.80 threshold require cautious interpretation.
title: CT-derived fractional flow reserve for anatomically long-segment coronary disease: a multicentre diagnostic accuracy study.

abstract:
PURPOSE: Sleep apnea (SA) is a highly prevalent condition in the United States and increases mortality risk in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI). We examined demographic and geographic national trends in mortality involving both SA and AMI from 2006 to 2023.
METHOD: This cross-sectional, population-based study used death certificates from the CDC WONDER database (2006-2023) mentioning both SA and AMI to assess mortality involving both conditions among adults aged ≥ 55 years using ICD-10 codes I21-I22 (AMI) and G47.3 (SA). Age-adjusted mortality rates (AAMRs) per million with 95% CIs were analyzed, and annual percentage changes (APCs) were calculated using Joinpoint regression across demographic and geographic subgroups.
RESULT: From 2006 to 2023, 18,388 deaths involving both SA and AMI occurred. While AMI-related mortality declined over time, mortality involving both SA and AMI increased. AAMRs involving both SA and AMI rose from 2006 to 2018 (APC: 5.07; 95% CI: 4.54 to 5.50), showed a steeper increase from 2018 to 2021 (APC: 13.71; 95% CI: 11.30 to 15.29), then declined by 2023 (APC:-6.46; 95% CI: -8.98 to -3.99). AAMRs among men were nearly three times those of women. Non-Hispanic (NH) Whites and NH Blacks had the highest AAMRs, while Hispanics had the lowest. The Midwest had the highest regional AAMR and the Northeast the lowest, while South Dakota and Nevada had the highest and lowest state-level AAMRs, respectively. From 2006 to 2020, rural areas showed higher AAMRs than urban areas.
CONCLUSION: While AMI-related mortality declined, mortality involving both SA and AMI increased from 2006 to 2021, with a decline from 2021 to 2023. Disparities persisted in men, NH Whites and NH Blacks, and those in the Midwest and rural areas. Whether targeted strategies, such as rigorous SA screening and prompt treatment, can reduce this growing burden warrants further study.
title: The growing burden of coexisting sleep apnea and acute myocardial infarction among adults aged 55 years and older in the United States, 2006-2023.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: In older patients with acute coronary syndromes (ACS), frailty predicts adverse outcomes, but whether radial access retains its lower complication rate in patients with frailty is unknown. We examined outcomes by access site and frailty status and whether frailty modified the association between access site and outcomes.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied 227 consecutive patients aged ≥ 70 years, irrespective of frailty status, who underwent percutaneous coronary intervention for ACS at a single center between January 2014 and June 2016. Frailty was screened at admission with the Dutch safety management system (Veiligheidsmanagementsysteem [VMS]) frailty instrument (frailty: VMS score ≥ 1). Primary endpoints were 1-year all-cause mortality and a 30-day composite outcome of death, vascular complications, bleeding, re-infarction and stroke. Effect modification was tested with interaction terms.
RESULTS: Access was femoral in 122 (53.7%) and radial in 105 (46.3%) patients. Of the 222 patients with a VMS score, 78 (35.1%) met frailty criteria. The 30-day composite endpoint occurred in 18.9% of patients with femoral access versus 3.8% with radial access (odds ratio [OR] 0.17, 95% confidence interval [CI] 0.06-0.51); 1-year mortality was 12.3% versus 6.7%, respectively (p = 0.14). The composite OR for radial access was 0.14 (95% CI 0.03-0.65) without frailty and 0.24 (95% CI 0.05-1.21) with frailty (ratio of ORs 1.70, 95% CI 0.19-15.54, p-interaction = 0.64; for 1-year mortality 1.24, 95% CI 0.19-8.33, p-interaction = 0.82). Frailty was associated with longer hospital stay and higher 1-year mortality adjusted for access site (hazard ratio [HR] 2.35, 95% CI 1.01-5.43), but not after further adjustment for age (HR 1.56, 95% CI 0.64-3.76).
CONCLUSION: Radial access was associated with markedly fewer early complications while frailty was associated with longer hospitalization and lower 1-year survival, largely explained by age. There was no statistically significant evidence of interaction between frailty and access site, although the interaction analysis was limited by the small number of events. These findings are to be considered hypothesis-generating.
title: Vascular Access Site, Frailty and Outcomes in Older Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention for Acute Coronary Syndromes.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Weaning patients from veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) after acute myocardial infarction-related cardiogenic shock (AMI-CS) depends on whether the injured left ventricle can recover. Cardiac magnetic resonance imaging is often impractical during ECMO support. Nuclear imaging may help, but its role in this unstable setting remains poorly defined.
METHODS: We report six consecutive male patients with AMI-CS and difficulty weaning from VA-ECMO who underwent myocardial perfusion emission computed tomography (ECT) and 18F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission computed tomography (18F-FDG PET-CT) during active support. The case series is used as a clinical entry point for a focused literature review of ECT/SPECT and FDG PET in myocardial viability assessment after myocardial infarction.
RESULTS: Imaging was completed in all six patients 12-22 days after ECMO initiation. No transfer- or scan-related adverse event was documented in the available record. Four patients had large estimated left ventricular perfusion defects (54%, 63%, 66%, and 59%) and were managed toward left ventricular assist device support or heart transplantation. One patient with a 41% defect died after withdrawal of life-sustaining therapy because of hepatic failure. One patient with a small estimated defect (4%) was successfully weaned. Prior studies indicate that FDG uptake and perfusion-metabolism mismatch are associated with regional functional recovery after revascularization, but patient-level decisions depend on revascularization, ventricular remodeling, end-organ function, and whether imaging results can be acted on safely.
CONCLUSIONS: ECT/18F-FDG PET-CT was feasible in this small VA-ECMO case series and provided perfusion and metabolic information when MRI was impractical. The evidence supports its use as an adjunct to clinical, echocardiographic, hemodynamic, and end-organ assessment, not as a stand-alone threshold for weaning, LVAD, or transplantation decisions.
title: ECT/18F-FDG PET-CT for myocardial viability assessment during VA-ECMO support in AMI-related cardiogenic shock: a case series and literature review.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Risk models for atrial fibrillation (AF) recurrence after catheter ablation apply the same predictor structure to every patient. This overlooks the biological differences between early and advanced disease. We examined whether the clinical predictors of 12-month recurrence differ across four disease-stage phenotypes.
METHODS: This retrospective cohort study enrolled 419 consecutive patients who underwent first-time radiofrequency ablation at Xiangya Hospital, Central South University, between October 2021 and June 2024. The institutional protocol was pulmonary vein isolation (PVI) alone, and patients undergoing concurrent left atrial appendage occlusion were excluded. Patients were classified by AF type and duration into four groups: early paroxysmal (Phenotype 1, ≤ 12 months, n = 225), long-standing paroxysmal (Phenotype 2, > 12 months, n = 86), recent-onset persistent (Phenotype 3, ≤ 18 months, n = 62), and long-duration persistent AF (Phenotype 4, > 18 months, n = 46). We performed phenotype-specific logistic regression, predictor × phenotype interaction testing, Kaplan-Meier and restricted mean survival analysis, and ROC analysis.
RESULTS: Twelve-month recurrence occurred in 88 patients (21.0%) and differed significantly across phenotypes (17.3%, 20.9%, 16.1%, and 45.7% in P1-P4; p < 0.001). Recurrence-free survival was worst in P4 (log-rank p < 0.001). In the overall model (AUC 0.672), the independent predictors were persistent AF type, longer duration, and hypertension, the last associated with lower recurrence. Phenotype-specific models revealed distinct profiles, and the sex × phenotype interaction was formally significant (p = 0.0042). In P1, younger age was the only predictor (AUC 0.701). In P3, female sex and hypertension were apparent predictors (apparent AUC 0.862; recurrence 43.8% in women vs. 6.5% in men), although this estimate is subject to optimism given only 10 events. In P4, no clinical variable was associated with recurrence despite its 45.7% rate, though power was insufficient to exclude moderate associations. The protective direction of hypertension strengthened across P1-P3 before disappearing in P4.
CONCLUSION: In this exploratory, single-center analysis, the clinical predictors of post-ablation AF recurrence appeared to shift across the four disease-stage phenotypes, with formal statistical support for sex. We propose the Predictor Lifecycle as a testable hypothesis for prospective, multicenter validation. These findings are hypothesis-generating and do not constitute a validated risk-stratification framework for clinical use.
title: Stage-dependent predictors of atrial fibrillation recurrence after catheter ablation: a proof-of-concept analysis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The effectiveness of reperfusion therapy in patients with myocardial infarction (MI) depends largely on timely treatment. This study aimed to compare treatment delays and in-hospital outcomes between self-transported and EMS-transported patients with STEMI.
METHODS: This retrospective observational cohort study included 208 patients with AMI who underwent PCI between March 2022 and June 2023. Of these, 92 patients arrived at the hospital by self-transport and 116 were transported by EMS. A p-value < 0.05 was considered statistically significant.
RESULTS: The study population was predominantly male (78.4%), with a mean age of 58.05 ± 12.06 years. Significant differences were observed between self-transported and EMS-transported patients in onset-to-door time (P < 0.001) and door-to-balloon time (P = 0.001). However, no significant differences were found in AMI-related complications, including stroke, cardiogenic shock, heart failure, pericarditis, and dysrhythmias. Likewise, in-hospital outcomes, including left ventricular ejection fraction, length of hospital stay, hospitalization costs, and mortality, did not differ significantly between the two groups.
CONCLUSION: Although EMS transport was associated with acceptably shorter treatment delays in patients with STEMI, total treatment times remained longer than recommended guideline targets. Our findings suggest that improving EMS utilization alone may be insufficient to improve clinical outcomes when overall system delays remain prolonged. However, given the limited sample size and low event rates, the results should be interpreted with caution. Patient-related factors may also influence treatment outcomes. Future large-scale studies are warranted to identify modifiable factors associated with treatment delays throughout the STEMI care pathway and to determine whether addressing these factors improves clinical outcomes.
title: Comparison of treatment delays and in-hospital outcomes between self-transported and EMS-transported patients with ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction undergoing PCI.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Distal transradial artery access (dTRA) is increasingly used for coronary interventions because it preserves proximal radial artery patency. However, effective hemostasis at the distal puncture site remains challenging due to the superficial vessel location and limited soft-tissue support. This study evaluated the hemostatic performance, local safety, patient-reported outcomes, and early radial artery patency of a novel distal radial artery compression device compared with conventional elastic bandage compression.
METHODS: In this prospective randomized controlled trial, 148 patients undergoing coronary angiography (CAG) or percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) via dTRA were randomized (1:1) to device-based or conventional compression. The primary outcome was first-attempt hemostasis success after compression release. Secondary outcomes included total hemostasis duration, operation time, access-site complications, pain, comfort, and ultrasound-assessed radial artery outcomes.
RESULTS: First-attempt hemostasis success was achieved in 74 patients (100.0%) in the device group and 70 patients (94.6%) in the elastic bandage group. Compared with elastic bandage compression, the novel device significantly shortened total hemostasis duration and operation time (both P < 0.001). Postoperative hand swelling was significantly less frequent and less severe in the device group (P < 0.001), while bleeding or hematoma formation was descriptively less frequent. No radial artery occlusion was detected by Doppler ultrasound before discharge in either group. Overall repeated-measures analysis showed no significant group effect or group-by-time interaction for pain or comfort scores.
CONCLUSIONS: The novel dTRA compression device achieved a high first-attempt hemostasis success rate and significantly shortened operation time and total hemostasis duration compared with conventional elastic bandage compression after CAG or PCI via dTRA. The device was associated with less postoperative hand swelling, while bleeding or hematoma formation was infrequent and should be interpreted cautiously. These findings support the short-term feasibility and procedural hemostatic efficiency of the device compared with conventional elastic bandage compression. Further multicenter studies incorporating standardized patent-hemostasis assessment, longer vascular follow-up, and comparisons with currently available dedicated distal radial compression devices are needed.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: Chinese Clinical Trial Registry, ChiCTR2500105403. Registered 2 July 2025.
title: A novel distal radial artery compression device versus elastic bandage compression after coronary angiography or percutaneous coronary intervention via distal transradial access: a prospective randomized controlled trial.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The 2025 European Society of Cardiology (ESC) and European Association for Cardio-Thoracic Surgery (EACTS) guidelines for valvular heart disease represent a pivotal update, emphasizing earlier intervention for aortic stenosis (AS) and broader indications for transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). These changes are driven by randomized trial data demonstrating TAVR's safety in lower-risk patients. However, as TAVR expands to younger cohorts, long-term durability remains a concern.
MAIN BODY: This narrative review examines key guideline updates for aortic valve disease, focusing on aortic stenosis (AS) and aortic regurgitation (AR), and integrates insights from recent registries (2020-2025) on TAVR explantation and redo-TAVR outcomes. Data from the EXPLANT-TAVR, EXPLANTORREDO-TAVR and FRANCE 2/FRANCE TAVI registries reveal reintervention rates of 0.3-1.7% at 8 years, with redo-TAVR offering superior short-term survival (30-day mortality 1.5-6.2%) compared to explantation (11.9-13.6%). Structural valve deterioration (SVD), leaflet thrombosis, and endocarditis predominate failure causes, underscoring the need for lifetime management strategies.
CONCLUSION: Implications include refined patient selection, enhanced imaging surveillance, and Heart Team-driven decisions to balance procedural benefits against reintervention risks.
title: New ESC/EACTS guidelines for the management of aortic valve disease: key takeaways and implications of long-term TAVR results based on recent explant and redo-TAVR registry outcomes.

abstract: Venous thromboembolism (VTE) carries substantial global morbidity and mortality, with 50%-60% of disease variability attributed to genetic factors. Hereditary antithrombin deficiency (HATD), caused by pathogenic variants in the SERPINC1 gene, is an autosomal dominant thrombophilia that confers a 20-40-fold higher risk of VTE, predominantly manifesting as recurrent pulmonary embolism (PE) and deep vein thrombosis (DVT). We report a 22-year-old male with recurrent PE secondary to type II HATD driven by a heterozygous SERPINC1 missense variant (c.1315 C > A, p.Pro439Thr). His second episode of PE progressed to obstructive cardiogenic shock refractory to systemic thrombolysis, accompanied by hemoptysis. Veno-arterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) was initiated, yet recurrent oxygenator thrombosis occurred despite high-dose unfractionated heparin (UFH) infusion. Laboratory testing revealed an antithrombin III (AT-III) activity level of 39.5%, confirming the diagnosis. Pulmonary angiography followed by mechanical thrombus aspiration was performed, and long-term anticoagulation was switched to rivaroxaban. The patient was successfully weaned from VA-ECMO, with no PE recurrence or adverse cardiovascular events recorded during 5 years of follow-up. This case represents the first published report of a young patient with a SERPINC1 variant complicated by recurrent high-risk PE unresponsive to rt-PA thrombolysis who survived after VA-ECMO-supported pulmonary thrombus aspiration. Early etiological genetic screening for hereditary thrombophilia is essential for managing refractory PE induced by SERPINC1 variants. Individualized regimens combining VA-ECMO, interventional thrombectomy, and direct oral anticoagulants (DOACs) yield favorable clinical outcomes and provide a reference for managing critically ill patients with hereditary thrombophilia.
title: SERPINC1-mediated hereditary antithrombin deficiency with refractory pulmonary embolism: successful treatment with VA-ECMO and interventional thrombus aspiration.

abstract: Iliac vein stent restenosis (ISR) remains a significant complication following stent placement for iliac vein compression syndrome (Rajput et al. in Cardiovasc Diagn Ther. 11:1103-1115, 2021) and post-thrombotic syndrome, with reported 1-year incidence rates of 18%-30%. This systematic review synthesizes evidence from the past five years to evaluate advances in predictive biomarker discovery, the concept of an optimal intervention window, and emerging therapeutic strategies. A comprehensive literature search identified 127 relevant studies. Our analysis reveals that combined biomarker models incorporating inflammatory cytokines (e.g., IL-6), microRNA panels (e.g., miR-92a/126), and coagulation-fibrosis markers (e.g., TAT, TGF-β1) show promising predictive value (pooled AUC up to 0.84), though clinical validation remains limited. Pathophysiological and computational modeling suggests a critical "subclinical stenosis phase" may exist 3-6 months post-stenting, during which interventions might be more effective, but robust clinical trial data supporting specific timing is scarce. While drug-eluting stents reduce short-term ISR rates, long-term safety concerns persist. Novel approaches, including bioresorbable materials and targeted biological therapies, are primarily in preclinical stages. This review underscores the urgent need for standardized biomarker validation, prospective trials to define intervention timing, and interdisciplinary collaboration to translate mechanistic insights into improved clinical outcomes for ISR prevention and management.
title: Biomarker screening and intervention window for iliac vein stent restenosis: a systematic review of evidence-based advances.

abstract: Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome (HCPS) due to Andes virus (ANDV) is a fulminant yet potentially reversible cause of respiratory and circulatory failure requiring timely critical care. This article addresses eleven practical questions on ICU management, drawing on clinical experience and research from the Chilean healthcare system. The recommendations cover early recognition, diagnostic workup, haemodynamic monitoring, cautious fluid and vasoactive support, respiratory management, VA-ECMO referral, daily ICU care, recovery, common pitfalls, and therapies with limited evidence. Because no antiviral or immunomodulatory therapy has consistently improved outcomes, survival relies on early suspicion, physiology-guided supportive care, and rapid escalation to ECMO-capable centres when severe cardiopulmonary failure develops.
title: Eleven questions on Hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome management in the ICU.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: The de Winter electrocardiographic pattern is a recognized equivalent of ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction and is most commonly associated with acute left anterior descending artery ischemia. Its coexistence with overt ST-segment elevation in another territory is uncommon and may create uncertainty in culprit-vessel identification. In patients with multivessel coronary disease and collateral-dependent myocardium, acute compromise of a donor coronary circulation may produce simultaneous but apparently discordant ECG manifestations.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 48-year-old man presented with worsening chest pain. The initial ECG showed a de Winter-like anterior morphology, characterized by upsloping J-point ST-segment depression followed by tall, symmetric T waves in leads V2-V4, together with ST-segment elevation in leads III and aVF. Urgent coronary angiography was delayed for approximately 4 h because the patient initially declined the procedure; aspirin, ticagrelor, and heparin were administered during this interval. At angiography, the left coronary circulation retained TIMI grade 3 antegrade flow but contained a critical proximal-to-mid left anterior descending artery lesion and severe distal left circumflex artery stenosis. The mid right coronary artery was completely occluded, with a blunt proximal stump and Rentrop grade 2 left-to-right collateral filling, strongly favoring a pre-existing RCA occlusion with chronic characteristics. Because the right coronary lesion was considered unlikely to be the acute culprit, emergency percutaneous coronary intervention was directed to the left anterior descending and distal left circumflex arteries. Inferior ST-segment elevation decreased markedly but incompletely after left coronary revascularization, with residual elevation most evident in lead III. The right coronary occlusion was successfully treated during a staged procedure 4 days later, after which the residual inferior ST-segment elevation decreased further.
CONCLUSIONS: De Winter-like anterior morphology and inferior ST-segment elevation may coexist when inferior myocardial perfusion depends on left-to-right collateral flow to a right coronary artery occlusion with features strongly favoring chronicity. This case raises the possibility of a dynamic donor-system ischemia mechanism as an explanation for the apparently discordant ECG findings. De Winter-like anterior morphology should not be disregarded solely because overt ST-segment elevation is present elsewhere. In this setting, the ST-elevation territory may not identify the vessel requiring first-pass reperfusion; ECG morphology should be integrated with angiographic chronicity features and collateral anatomy.
title: Suspected donor-vessel ischemia in a collateral-dependent right coronary artery occlusion presenting as a de Winter-like pattern with inferior ST-segment elevation: a case report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Magnesium (Mg) is an essential electrolyte that plays a critical role in cardiovascular physiology. Several studies have investigated the relationship between Mg levels and cardiovascular outcomes; however, the findings have been inconsistent. Therefore, this study aims to investigate the association between serum magnesium levels and short- to medium-term cardiovascular events in patients with acute myocardial infarction (AMI) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
METHODS: This prospective cohort study was conducted at the Isfahan Cardiovascular Research Institute, Isfahan, Iran, between October 2018 and September 2023, within the framework of the Persian Cardiovascular Disease Registry. Patients were followed for short-term (1-month and 6-month) and medium-term (12-month) major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) after PCI and were categorized into three groups according to their admission serum magnesium levels: < 1.8 mg/dL, 1.8-2.2 mg/dL, and > 2.2 mg/dL.
RESULTS: A total of 3,640 of the 5,300 patients with a confirmed diagnosis of AMI who underwent PCI met the eligibility criteria and were included in the final analysis. The mean age of the study population was 64.70 ± 12.07 years, and 80.3% of participants were male. At the 6-month follow-up, mortality was significantly higher among patients with serum Mg levels > 2.2 mg/dL (odds ratio [OR] = 1.45, P = 0.02). In contrast, at the 12-month follow-up, mortality was significantly higher among patients with serum Mg levels < 1.8 mg/dL (OR = 1.59, P < 0.01). The incidence of MACE was significantly higher among patients with serum Mg levels < 1.8 mg/dL at the 12-month follow-up (OR = 1.61, P < 0.01).
CONCLUSION: Among patients with AMI undergoing PCI, both hypomagnesemia and hypermagnesemia were associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes during follow-up. Hypomagnesemia was associated with an increased risk of medium-term mortality and major adverse cardiovascular events, whereas hypermagnesemia was associated with increased short-term mortality. These findings suggest a potential U-shaped association between serum magnesium levels and cardiovascular outcomes in this high-risk population. As this was an observational study, these findings reflect associations rather than causal relationships. Further prospective studies are warranted to confirm these associations before any clinical application is considered.
title: Magnesium levels and short- to medium-term cardiovascular events after percutaneous coronary intervention: a prospective cohort study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute profound thrombocytopenia is a rare, yet potentially life-threatening complication associated with intravenous glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptor inhibitors (GPI), which are widely used in the management of acute coronary syndrome and during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). Treatments with steroids and intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIg) are recommended for GPI-induced thrombocytopenia; however, evidence regarding their efficacy remains limited.
METHODS: In this retrospective study, 21 patients who developed acute profound thrombocytopenia (defined as a platelet count < 20 × 109/L) following PCI and GPI treatment were enrolled. Patients' clinical characteristics, the timing of detection of thrombocytopenia, the administration of steroids and IVIg therapy, and subsequent changes in platelet counts and clinical outcomes were analyzed.
RESULTS: Among the 21 patients, 7 were females, and the median age was 63 years. Tirofiban and eptifibatide were administered to 12 and 9 patients, respectively. Thrombocytopenia was detected on the day of PCI in 9 patients. Among the remaining 12 patients, one was found to have a profound decline in platelets only after the onset of intracerebral hemorrhage and coma, whereas the other 11 patients were diagnosed during routine blood testing on the first day after PCI. The median nadir platelet count was 4 × 109/L among all patients. 11 patients received both steroids and IVIg, 6 received steroids alone, and 4 did not receive any intervention. To evaluate the potential effect of steroids and IVIg therapy on platelet recovery, patients were categorized into three treatment groups: Steroids plus IVIg, steroids alone, and no intervention. No statistical difference was observed among the treatment groups. A separate analysis was performed by categorizing patients according to whether thrombocytopenia was detected on the day of PCI (early detection group) or on the first day after PCI (late detection group). Patients with early diagnosis who underwent prompt GPI withdrawal demonstrated significantly faster platelet recovery. The median time to platelet recovery above 20 × 109/L was significantly shorter in the early detection group (24 h) than in the late detection group (72 h), with a p-value of 0.017.
CONCLUSIONS: GPI-induced thrombocytopenia progresses rapidly following GPI exposure and is marked by an abrupt onset. Timely detection of thrombocytopenia and prompt GPI withdrawal are critical for platelet recovery. In our study, neither steroids nor IVIg improved platelet recovery.
title: Acute profound thrombocytopenia associated with glycoprotein IIb/IIIa receptor inhibitor after percutaneous coronary intervention: a single-center 6-year case series and therapy insights.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Hyperinsulinemia is an early metabolic abnormality commonly associated with insulin resistance, but its relationship with cardiovascular injury in real-world populations remains incompletely understood. We examined whether fasting insulin is related to arterial stiffening and early myocardial biomarker abnormalities in a large health-examination population.
METHODS: This real-world retrospective analysis enrolled 30,343 adults who received routine health examinations from January 2017 to November 2021. For individuals with multiple visits, the earliest examination was used as the baseline record. Fasting insulin was evaluated in quartile categories, a log-transformed continuous exposure, and a hyperinsulinemia indicator based on the cohort-specific 75th percentile. The binary arterial-stiffness endpoint was defined using a mean baPWV (brachial-ankle pulse wave velocity) threshold of 1400 cm/s or higher. Myocardial injury was evaluated by cardiac troponin I or T. Logistic regression models were fitted to quantify the relationships of fasting insulin and HOMA-IR (homeostatic model assessment of insulin resistance) with baPWV-related outcomes and myocardial injury markers. Dose-response patterns were explored using restricted cubic spline modeling. Subgroup analysis and sensitivity analysis were performed. Python (3.13.0) was used for statistical analysis.
RESULTS: Higher insulin categories were accompanied by greater adiposity, blood pressure, glucose, HOMA-IR, triglycerides, baPWV, and arterial-stiffness. Hyperinsulinemia was correlated with arterial stiffness in the unadjusted model and adjusted model (OR, 1.31; 95% CI, 1.22-1.40, P < 0.001). Compared with the lowest insulin quartile, the highest quartile was associated with markedly increased odds of arterial stiffness (OR, 1.56; 95% CI, 1.41-1.74, P < 0.001). Spline curves indicated that fasting insulin and HOMA-IR were positively and non-linearly related to mean baPWV. In contrast, the association between hyperinsulinemia and composite myocardial injury was not statistically significant.
CONCLUSIONS: In this large real-world health examination cohort, hyperinsulinemia was independently and consistently associated with increased arterial stiffness. However, its association with subclinical myocardial injury was weaker. These results support fasting insulin as a potential early metabolic indicator of vascular stiffening, whereas its relationship with myocardial injury requires further longitudinal investigation.
title: Hyperinsulinemia and its associations with arterial stiffness and myocardial injury: a real-world cohort study.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study investigated the association between multiple frailty-related markers-Clinical Frailty Scale (CFS), Controlling Nutritional Status (CONUT) score, and computed tomography (CT)-based sarcopenia-and overall survival after aortic valve replacement (AVR) for severe aortic stenosis (AS), with particular emphasis on the first year after AVR.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: A total of 407 patients with severe AS who underwent surgical or transcatheter AVR at a tertiary center between November 2020 and December 2022 were retrospectively included. Three frailty-related markers were analyzed: CFS score for functional frailty, CONUT score for nutritional status, and CT-defined sarcopenia for structural muscle depletion. The CONUT score was calculated using serum markers, and sarcopenia was defined according to cohort-specific tertiles of the paravertebral muscle index quantified at the 12th thoracic vertebra (T12) vertebral level using CT. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards analysis was performed to assess the prognostic associations of the Society of Thoracic Surgeons (STS) score and the three frailty-related markers with all-cause mortality after AVR.
RESULTS: Within 1 year after AVR, 32 patients (7.9%) died. In the overall multivariable analysis, higher CFS scores and CT-defined sarcopenia were independently associated with mortality, with hazard ratios (HRs) of 1.82 (95% confidence interval [CI], 1.40-2.38; P < 0.001) and 2.63 (95% CI, 1.22-5.67; P = 0.014), respectively. The STS score and CONUT scores were not associated with survival, with HRs of 1.00 (95% CI, 0.95-1.06; P = 0.883) and 1.05 (95% CI, 0.90-1.22; P = 0.563), respectively. A significant interaction was observed between the CONUT score and sarcopenia.
CONCLUSION: Among patients with severe AS undergoing AVR, higher CFS scores and CT-based sarcopenia were independently associated with survival after adjustment for the STS score. The prognostic association of the CONUT score differed according to sarcopenia status. These findings support the incorporation of functional and structural vulnerabilities into risk assessment for patients undergoing AVR for AS; however, the role of nutritional status requires further investigation.
title: Association of CT-Based Sarcopenia, Clinical Frailty, and Nutritional Status With Mortality After Aortic Valve Replacement for Severe Aortic Stenosis.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Acute myocardial infarction (AMI) is a critical condition resulting from coronary occlusion, leading to myocardial necrosis and dysfunction. Protein posttranslational modifications (PTMs) regulate key inflammatory and signaling pathways in its pathogenesis. Accordingly, exploring transcriptomic signatures of genes encoding PTM-regulatory factors may provide valuable insights for improving early diagnosis and therapeutic stratification in AMI.
METHODS: Candidate genes were obtained by integrating transcriptomic data on AMI from public databases with a previously published gene set encoding regulators for 20 categories of protein PTMs. Differentially expressed genes (DEGs) were intersected with this PTM-regulator gene set to identify PTM-related DEGs. Machine learning approaches together with expression analyses were employed to identify diagnostic biomarkers. Their potential mechanisms were systematically elucidated via multidimensional analyses, including deep neural network (DNN) model construction, biological pathway analysis, immune landscape profiling, regulatory network reconstruction, and therapeutic compound prioritization. Clinical validation of the key biomarkers was performed using RT-qPCR.
RESULTS: This study identified three biomarkers among PTM-regulator-related genes for AMI: GABARAPL1, PELI1, and NLRP3. Enrichment profiling showed that all three biomarkers were prominently linked to pathways related to Leishmania infection. Correlation analysis of immune cell profiles showed that all three biomarkers were most strongly associated with plasmacytoid dendritic cells. Molecular regulatory network analysis uncovered their associated transcription factors, targeted miRNAs, and lncRNA interaction networks. Drug prediction and molecular docking identified several potential targeting compounds, among which 1,4-chrysenequinone exhibited docking scores of -7 kcal/mol and -8.9 kcal/mol with GABARAPL1 and PELI1, respectively, while calcitriol showed a docking score of -10.1 kcal/mol with NLRP3, indicating strong predicted binding affinity. RT-qPCR clinical validation confirmed significant upregulation of GABARAPL1, PELI1, and NLRP3 in AMI patients (all P < 0.01), consistent with the integrative multi-omics findings.
CONCLUSION: Using transcriptome-based bioinformatics, this study identified and validated three transcriptomic biomarkers (GABARAPL1, PELI1, and NLRP3) among genes encoding PTM-regulatory factors for AMI, offering molecular resources for future investigations into diagnostic and therapeutic targets in AMI.
title: Exploring biomarkers and regulatory mechanisms associated with 20 protein post-translational modifications in acute myocardial infarction based on transcriptomics.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is a highly malignant neuroendocrine tumor with rapid progression and poor prognosis. Pathological examination is the gold standard for its diagnosis, yet pathological sampling is unfeasible in some clinical scenarios due to various constraints, making imaging and tumor markers critical for clinical decision-making. This two-case report describes the typical computed tomography (CT) findings of SCLC and explores the clinical value of combining CT imaging with tumor markers in guiding the diagnosis and treatment of SCLC patients for whom pathological confirmation is not feasible.
CASE REPORT: We report two SCLC cases: Case 1 was a 56-year-old male with pathologically confirmed SCLC who presented typical imaging findings of hilar and mediastinal fused lymph nodes and achieved a partial response after combined chemoradiotherapy. Case 2 was a 67-year-old male with chest tightness and hemoptysis for 2 months, whose chest CT showed fused lymph nodes (a typical SCLC feature) and markedly elevated neuron-specific enolase (NSE: 221 ng/mL; reference range 1-16.2 ng/mL). Biopsy was unfeasible due to recent coronary stenting and ongoing antiplatelet therapy, and a clinical diagnosis of limited-stage SCLC was made via a combination of typical CT imaging features, significantly elevated NSE and clinical symptoms. The patient received timely EC regimen chemotherapy and subsequent standard chemoradiotherapy, which resulted in a clinical complete response (CR).
CONCLUSIONS: This case report details the typical CT manifestations of SCLC and demonstrates that the combined application of typical CT findings, tumor markers and clinical symptoms may provide a pragmatic basis for timely clinical diagnosis and treatment of SCLC patients when pathological sampling is not achievable. This approach may help avoid treatment delay and improve clinical outcomes for such patients, while emphasizing that pathological examination remains the gold standard for SCLC diagnosis.
title: Two case reports of small cell lung cancer: typical CT manifestations, with one case illustrating adjunctive CT-based diagnosis without pathological confirmation.

abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Transcatheter valve implantation is a cutting-edge technology for high and low risk patients with aortic stenosis. Bioprosthetic valves are limited due to several disadvantages as a long-term durability and structural valve degeneration. Polymeric aortic valve leaflet devices represent state-of-the-art technology to overcome limitations of bioprostheses. Nevertheless, more recent biocompatible and biostable polymers have revealed a significant potential. Additionally, 3D additive manufacturing opens new paths for patient-specific design of biomedical implants. Flexible polymers may not only mimic native aortic valve, but also may improve long-term durability. Polyurethanes and styrene polymers are promising materials for modern polymer valves. Nevertheless, mechanical properties of additive manufactured TPU or SEBS leaflets are not properly studied.
METHODS: Experimental study of TPU and SEBS samples and aortic valve leaflets for novel aortic valve polymer TAVI prosthesis is presented. Tensile tests and compression tests of three types of FDM-printed samples with various filament alignments (axial alignment, transversal alignment, diagonal alignment) were performed. The results of tests confirmed that longitudinal axial alignment achieve a maximum stress compared to transversal and diagonal directions. Compressive tests of TPU and SEBS 3D-manufactured aortic valve leaflets with digital image correlation technology were performed. Young's modulus and Poisson's ratio were evaluated. Moreover, parameters of constitutive models were found.
RESULTS: The TPU tensile specimen exhibits the highest stress/strain values at a speed of 100 mm/min, regardless of the filament alignment pattern. Slightly lower results are observed at a speed of 50 mm/min, which is likely associated with a wide range of plastic deformation. In the case of SEBS, a different pattern is observed: at 500 mm/min, it demonstrates high resistance to fracture, unlike TPU. A comparison of TPU and SEBS specimens at the same speeds and with the same alignment, based on maximum stress values, shows a minimal difference of 4% with the axial alignment at a speed of 50 mm/min; however, when comparing strains, the difference increases to 90%. The results of the compression experiment on aortic valve specimens made of TPU and SEBS at a speed of 30 mm/min showed that TPU force values for is considerably lower (4% of the maximum case), while for SEBS the spread increases to 20% of the maximum case.
CONCLUSION: SEBS aortic valve leaflets were shown to be stiffer than TPU. It can be a step for choice of stiffer/softer leaflets for patient-specific device.
