abstract:
BACKGROUND: Focal myopericarditis is an uncommon inflammatory condition that may present with localized ST-segment elevation and closely mimic ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), creating a diagnostic challenge in acute cardiovascular care.
CASE SUMMARY: A 53-year-old man presented with acute pleuritic chest pain radiating to the back, worsened by inspiration and the supine position, and relieved by sitting upright. Electrocardiography demonstrated concave ST-segment elevation in the inferior leads, raising suspicion for inferior STEMI. Urgent coronary angiography revealed nonobstructive coronary artery disease without a culprit lesion. Persistent ST-segment elevation and atypical clinical features prompted cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) imaging, which demonstrated myocardial edema, subepicardial late gadolinium enhancement, and mild pericardial effusion, confirming focal myopericarditis.
DISCUSSION: This case emphasizes the importance of integrating clinical, angiographic, and CMR findings to distinguish focal myopericarditis from STEMI and ensure appropriate management.
TAKE-HOME MESSAGE: CMR imaging is essential for differentiating inflammatory myocardial injury from acute myocardial infarction.
title: Diagnostic Challenge of Focal Myopericarditis Mimicking Inferior STEMI: When the ECG Misleads.
Reply to "Does statistical significance demonstrate a change in prognostic utility after TAVI?".

abstract: Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction (LVOTO) remains one of the most catastrophic complications of transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) interventions, including TMVR in native valve, valve-in-valve, valve-in-ring, and valve-in-mitral annular calcification procedures. Its incidence varies widely across procedural types (0%-40%), with mortality rates approaching 36%, and represents a leading cause of patient ineligibility, excluding 4%-50% of candidates from TMVR. Accurate pre-procedural risk stratification relies on cardiac computed tomography, which enables annular sizing, virtual valve implantation, neo- and skirt neo-left ventricular outflow tract area quantification, and fluoroscopic projection planning. Key anatomic determinants of LVOTO include anterior mitral leaflet length, aortomitral angle, septal hypertrophy, left ventricular cavity size, and device-related factors. To mitigate LVOTO risk and expand treatment eligibility, in addition to septal modification, anterior mitral leaflet modification techniques have emerged, broadly categorized into electrosurgical laceration approaches-LAMPOON and ELASTA-and balloon-assisted translocation techniques for balloon-expandable valves-BATMAN, CLEVE, DETROIT, and ROBIN. Each strategy addresses distinct anatomic substrates and procedural scenarios, and their complementary profiles support individualized technique selection. This review aims to present an in-depth discussion of LVOTO in TMVR and anterior leaflet modification strategies.
title: Left ventricular outflow tract obstruction in transcatheter mitral interventions: percutaneous anterior leaflet modification.

abstract: Atherosclerotic plaque healing is a dynamic biological mechanism that occurrs after plaque disruption and represents an endogenous reparative response within the atherosclerotic lesion. This process unfolds through three partially overlapping phases: endogenous thrombus lysis, granulation tissue formation, and re-endothelialization. Through the coordinated interaction of circulating cells, vascular wall components, and soluble mediators, plaque healing promotes fibrous repair and structural stabilization of the disrupted plaque. For many years, plaque healing remained primarily a histopathological observation described in post-mortem studies. The advent of high-resolution intracoronary imaging, particularly optical coherence tomography, has enabled in vivo visualization of the characteristic layered morphology of healed plaques, providing direct clinical confirmation of these early pathological findings. These observations have significantly improved our understanding of the clinical significance of plaque healing. Healed plaques are more frequently observed in patients with chronic coronary syndromes, supporting the concept that healing contributes to plaque stabilization. At the same time, recurrent cycles of plaque disruption followed by repair may lead to progressive luminal narrowing, thereby contributing to the long-term progression of coronary atherosclerosis. This review provided an updated overview of the clinical significance and implications of healed plaques in coronary artery disease, the mechanisms underlying plaque healing, and examines emerging intracoronary and non-invasive imaging modalities that allow their in vivo identification.
title: Atherosclerotic plaque healing: mechanisms and clinical relevance.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (VA-ECMO) provided temporary circulatory support in refractory cardiogenic shock but substantially altered ventricular preload, afterload, and native ejection. Consequently, conventional echocardiographic measurements obtained during support did not necessarily represent intrinsic myocardial contractility. This scoping review mapped conventional and advanced echocardiographic approaches used to characterize myocardial recovery and guide VA-ECMO liberation.
METHODS: PubMed, OpenAlex, and Crossref were searched from inception through September 20, 2026. Eligible studies included adults receiving VA-ECMO in whom echocardiography was used to assess myocardial recovery, flow-dependent cardiac performance, weaning readiness, decannulation outcomes, or transition to durable mechanical support. Citation searching supplemented the database searches. Study selection was reported according to PRISMA-ScR, and the search process was documented according to PRISMA-S. Data were synthesized descriptively because of substantial heterogeneity in populations, imaging protocols, flow-reduction strategies, and outcome definitions.
RESULTS: The searches identified 3,912 records, of which 2,834 remained after duplicate removal. Thirty-nine full-text reports were assessed, and 35 studies were included. Conventional measures, particularly left ventricular ejection fraction and left ventricular outflow tract velocity-time integral, were frequently associated with successful weaning but were strongly influenced by ECMO-related loading conditions. Flow reduction commonly improved ejection fraction, longitudinal strain, native stroke output, and annular velocities without representing immediate biological myocardial recovery. Advanced phenotyping incorporated left ventricular global longitudinal strain, mitral annular plane systolic excursion, cardiac time intervals, left atrial reservoir strain, right ventricular free-wall strain, three-dimensional right ventricular ejection fraction, and right ventricular-pulmonary arterial coupling. Serial and flow-challenge assessments provided greater prognostic information than isolated measurements under full support. Distinct trajectories included coordinated biventricular recovery, isolated left ventricular recovery, persistent biventricular failure, and refractory systolic stagnation. Successful decannulation did not consistently predict sustained recovery or survival, and integrated models combining echocardiography with pulsatility, filling pressures, vasoactive requirements, and end-organ recovery showed the greatest clinical utility.
CONCLUSIONS: Echocardiographic assessment of myocardial recovery during VA-ECMO had evolved from static ventricular thresholds toward dynamic, multiparametric phenotyping. No single parameter reliably established decannulation readiness. Standardized serial imaging and controlled flow-reduction protocols that integrated biventricular function, deformation, native forward flow, ventricular-vascular coupling, filling pressures, and clinical stability were required. Prospective multicenter validation and harmonized definitions of sustained myocardial recovery remained necessary.
title: Advanced Echocardiographic Phenotyping of Myocardial Recovery During VA-ECMO-A Scoping Review.

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: The C-reactive protein-triglyceride glucose index (CTI) has been associated with cardiovascular risk. This study evaluated its prognostic value for repeat revascularization and in-stent restenosis (ISR) in patients with chronic coronary syndrome (CCS) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI).
METHODS: A total of 2147 CCS patients undergoing PCI were stratified into CTI tertiles. The primary endpoint was a composite of repeat revascularization and ISR. Kaplan-Meier analysis with log-rank tests was used to compare event rates. Multivariable Cox proportional hazards models and restricted cubic spline analyses were applied to assess associations. Predictive performance was evaluated using time-dependent receiver operating characteristic curves.
RESULTS: During a median follow-up of 60 months, 992 patients (46.2%) experienced the primary endpoint. Event rates increased progressively across CTI tertiles. After multivariable adjustment, CTI remained independently associated with the primary endpoint (HR 1.11; 95% CI 1.01-1.22; p = 0.028). Compared with the lowest tertile, the highest CTI tertile was associated with a 31% higher risk (HR 1.31; 95% CI 1.10-1.55; p = 0.002). A linear dose-response relationship was observed (p for non-linearity = 0.172; p overall = 0.040). The multivariable model incorporating CTI showed modest discrimination, with AUCs of 0.627 (95% CI 0.602-0.651) at 3 years and 0.651 (95% CI 0.627-0.674) at 5 years.
CONCLUSIONS: CTI is independently associated with increased risks of repeat revascularization and ISR after PCI in patients with CCS. However, its incremental predictive value beyond conventional risk factors appears limited and requires further validation.
title: Inflammatory and Insulin Resistance Indicator for Predicting Repeat Revascularization and In-Stent Restenosis in Patients With Chronic Coronary Syndrome Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention.

abstract: In acute central retinal artery occlusion (CRAO), vessel stenosis and hemodynamic impairment significantly affect visual prognosis. We report a 69-year-old man who presented with 18 hours of acute, severe right eye blurred vision. Fundus examination and optical coherence tomography confirmed central retinal artery (CRA) occlusion with inner retinal edema. Digital subtraction angiography revealed an aortic arch variation and severe C1 segment stenosis of the right internal carotid artery (ICA), accompanied by delayed ophthalmic artery filling and faint visualization of the CRA. After multidisciplinary consultation, the patient underwent ICA stenting. Postoperative imaging showed resolved stenosis and improved retinal perfusion; the patient's vision subsequently improved and stabilized. This case suggests that revascularization can facilitate visual recovery even beyond the traditional window. Furthermore, faint CRA visualization on digital subtraction angiography indicates residual flow, providing a potential rationale for recanalization therapy.
title: Pearls & Oy-sters: Trace Visualization of the Central Retinal Artery: A Favorable Sign for Late-Window Endovascular Therapy in Central Retinal Artery Occlusion.

abstract:
INTRODUCTION: To investigate the ability of the baseline C-reactive protein-to-serum Albumin Ratio (CAR) to assess current vasculitis activity and predict subsequent complications in patients with antineutrophil cytoplasmic Antibody-Associated Vasculitis (AAV).
METHODS: Data from the medical records of 319 patients with AAV were retrospectively reviewed. High activity was defined as the highest tertile of the Birmingham Vasculitis Activity Score (BVAS). All-Cause Mortality (ACM), relapse, End-Stage Kidney Disease (ESKD), Cerebrovascular Accident (CVA), and Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) were evaluated as subsequent complications. ACM, ESKD, and CVA with significant Areas Under the Curve (AUC) in receiver operating characteristic curve analysis, were investigated.
RESULTS: The median age of the study subjects (64.6% females) was 60.0-years. Baseline CAR was independently correlated with current BVAS and yielded the numerically largest AUC for high activity. Patients with baseline CAR ≥ 3.07, ≥ 1.26, and ≥ 14.01 exhibited significantly higher Relative Risks (RR) for ACM (RR = 8.017), ESKD (RR = 3.270), and CVA (RR = 6.660) than those with baseline CAR < 3.07, < 1.26, and < 14.01, respectively. Additionally, patients with baseline CAR ≥ 3.07, ≥ 1.26, and ≥ 14.01 showed reduced cumulative patient, ESKD-free, and CVA-free survival rates compared with those with baseline CAR < 3.07, < 1.26, and < 14.01, respectively. Multivariable Cox proportional analysis revealed that baseline CAR and its complication-related cut-offs were independently associated with subsequent ACM, ESKD, and CVA, except for baseline CAR ≥ 1.26 for ESKD.
CONCLUSIONS: Baseline CAR demonstrated the multipotent ability to reflect current high activity (the highest tertile of BVAS) and predict subsequent ACM, ESKD, and CVA in patients with AAV.
title: Multipotent ability of the baseline C-reactive protein-to-serum Albumin Ratio (CAR) to assess current activity and predict subsequent complications of ANCA-associated vasculitis.

abstract: Cardiac troponins are definitive biomarkers of acute myocardial infarction (AMI). However, current diagnostic assays quantify the overall immunoreactive concentration of these biomarkers without distinguishing between their different circulating forms. After myocardial injury, troponins are primarily released as cTnI-T-C complexes, which gradually dissociate into subunits, such as free cTnI. Previous studies have suggested that the cTnI:cTnI-T-C ratio may function as a "molecular clock" for estimating the onset of AMI, necessitating precise analytical differentiation between the different troponin forms. Herein, we present a shear horizontal surface acoustic wave (SH-SAW) biosensor platform that can quantify these ratios in a single measurement. This approach leverages the simultaneous amplitude and phase changes in acoustic wave propagation, which provide complementary information on the spatial extent and acoustic properties of surface-bound molecular layers. The layer parameter (lp), derived from the attenuation and velocity responses, was used to characterize the surface-bound protein layer. Using a guided configuration and analytical multiparametric model, we determined the layer parameters for intact cTnI-T-C, free cTnI, and their mixtures. The layer parameter exhibited a systematic nonlinear dependence on the cTnI:cTnI-T-C molar ratio, enabling the estimation of this ratio without prior knowledge of the total protein concentration. Combined with composition-dependent calibration, this approach provides a framework for determining both the troponin molecular composition and total concentration. Beyond its potential application in the temporal characterization of AMI, the proposed strategy may be extended to other biomarkers for which discrimination between molecular forms provides diagnostically relevant information.
title: Single-step determination of cardiac troponin molecular form ratios using multiparametric SH-SAW biosensing.

abstract: In a 60-year-old man with a history of stroke, coronary angiography revealed triple vessel disease, comprising left anterior descending artery (LAD) #6-7 with 99% diffuse stenosis within the stent, #11 and #12 with 90% stenosis, and right coronary artery (RCA) #1 stent with 50% stenosis. Cardiac ultrasonography showed 34% left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF) without mitral regurgitation (MR) or tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Following median sternotomy, the bilateral internal thoracic artery (BITA) was harvested by skeletonization;however, dissection was confirmed at the distal end of the right internal thoracic artery (RITA). Owing to severe apical adhesions, we decided to perform on-pump beating coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) for this patient. Cardiopulmonary bypass was initiated via proximal aortic arch inflow and bicaval drainage without left ventricule (LV) venting. Subsequently, a left internal thoracic surgery (LITA)-free RITA composite Y-graft was prepared. On-pump beating CABG was performed in the graft design of the LITA-LAD (onlay patch, 4.5 cm), LITA-free RITA composite Y-graft to the obtuse marginal (OM) artery, and AO-saphenous vein graft (SVG)-4 posterior descending artery (PD)-4AV by sequential anastomosis. Many inflammatory cells invaded the RITA and coronary artery, and distal vessel thickening was confirmed but not in the ascending aorta. Coronary arteritis induced by myeloproliferative neoplasms was diagnosed based on pathology. Coronary computed tomography (CT) revealed the patency of all grafts.
journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
title: [Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting for Coronary Arteritis Induced by Myeloproliferative Neoplasms:Report of a Case].

abstract: A two-month-old girl presented with hyperpnea, a significant cardiac murmur, and severe hypoxemia. Transthoracic echocardiography at the referring hospital suggested congenital heart disease with highflow pulmonary hypertension, and she was referred to our institution for further evaluation. At our hospital, echocardiography demonstrated transposition of the great arteries (TGA) with a small ventricular septal defect (VSD), atrial septal defect, and patent ductus arteriosus. Detailed echocardiography revealed that the aorta was positioned slightly posterior and to the right of the pulmonary artery, with the presence of both subpulmonary and subaortic conus. The subaortic conus represented an atypical anatomical feature of posterior TGA. Based on these findings, a diagnosis of posterior TGA with bilateral conus was established. Aortic angiography demonstrated a Shaher type 9 pattern, in which the right coronary artery courses anterior to the aorta and the left coronary artery passes posterior to the pulmonary artery. At three months of age, she underwent an arterial switch operation. The Lecompte maneuver was not performed because the aorta was positioned posterior and to the right of the pulmonary artery (original Jatene procedure). An autologous pericardial patch was interposed along the left margin of the pulmonary artery bifurcation stump to shift the anastomotic site of the neo-pulmonary artery rightward, thereby preventing compression of the transferred coronary arteries. A small VSD intentionally left open as a fenestration in anticipation of a postoperative pulmonary hypertensive crisis. The postoperative course was uneventful.
journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
title: [Surgical Case of Posterior Transposition of the Great Arteries with Bilateral Conus].

abstract: We report a rare case of acute mitral regurgitation following blunt chest trauma. A 48-year-old man with a history of ventricular septal defect repair in childhood had a traffic accident and was hit in the anterior chest. Initial evaluation at a local hospital showed no abnormalities, and echocardiography was not performed. Seven days later, he developed dyspnea and acute heart failure and was referred to our hospital. Transthoracic echocardiography revealed severe mitral regurgitation caused by chordae rupture and P2-3 prolapse. After conservative treatment for heart failure, mitral valve repair using artificial chordae and annuloplasty was successfully performed, along with a David procedure for concomitant aortic root dilatation. The postoperative course was uneventful, and mitral valve function has remained satisfactory for more than one year. This case highlights the importance of early echocardiographic assessment after blunt chest trauma, even when initial clinical findings are unremarkable, to enable timely diagnosis and preservation of the native mitral valve.
journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
title: [Mitral Valve Repair for Traumatic Mitral Regurgitation Following a Traffic Injury].

abstract:
OBJECTIVE: To ensure a high level of safety in right mini-thoracotomy [minimally invasive cardiac surgery (MICS)-Mitral], risk assessment of MICS-Mitral-specific complications and appropriate patient selection are required. The author has created a risk prediction formula from 3,250 MICS-Mitral cases in the Japan Cardiovascular Surgery Database (JCVSD)[Circulation J 2019] and has experience in establishing MICS program in local hospitals three times. This study examined the validity and safety of case selection using the risk prediction formula for MICS cases actually performed at each facility.
PATIENTS AND METHODS: The subjects were 123 cases that met the criteria for the risk prediction formula from 2014 to 2024. For each case, the risk of surgical mortality and composite outcome (mortality, stroke, and re-exploration for bleeding) were calculated using the risk prediction formula and compared with surgical outcomes.
RESULTS: 1The predicted mortality rate for all cases was 1.0%, and the composite outcome was 6.8%, which was significantly lower than that of median sternotomy cases at the same time. 2There was no mortality, and no stoke was observed, but there were two cases of re-exploration for bleeding, one case of re-expansion pulmonary edema, one case requiring pereutaneous cardiopulmonary support (PCPS) due to poor venous drainage, and one case requiring prolonged ventilation and intraaortic balloon pumping (IABP). 3In cases with a precited composite outcome of less than 10%, the complication rate was 1.9%, while in cases with a predicted composite outcome of 10% or more, these complications tended to be higher at 25%. 4The incidence of complications has been decreasing in the recent hospital.
CONCLUSION: Cases with low risk scores are suitable for MICS, no surgical deaths were observed in MICS cases, and serious complications were frequently seen in cases with a predicted composite outcome of 10% or more. The risk prediction formula was considered useful for appropriate patient selection.
journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
title: [Assessment of Patient Selection and Safety Using Risk Calculator in Patients who Underwent Minimally Invasive Mitral Valve Surgery].

abstract: We have actively adopted minimally invasive mitral valve plasty (MICS-MVP) since the early phase of its introduction. Between October 2012 and March 2021, we performed MICS-MVP in 264 patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation. The mean age was 58.5 (range, 18~82) years;104 patients (39 %) were female, and 60 patients had concomitant atrial fibrillation. Concomitant procedures were performed in 150 patients, including tricuspid valve surgery in 56 patients, arrhythmia surgery in 59, left atrial appendage procedures in 58, and congenital heart disease surgery in 39. The mean operative time was 254 minutes. Regarding repair techniques, artificial chordae were used in 139 cases;annuloplasty was performed using a full ring in 101 cases and a partial band in 162 cases. The 5-year survival rate was 98.1%, and the 5-year freedom from major adverse cardiac and cerebrovascular events (MACCE) was 92.8%. There were no cardiac deaths, and 7 readmissions for heart failure. Compared with the fullring group, the partial-band group showed a significantly lower mean mitral valve pressure gradient (p<0.001). By multivariable analysis for MACCE incidence and readmission for heart failure, none of the factors-including surgical technique and choice of annuloplasty device-were detected as significant predictors. In recent years, annuloplasty with partial band and artificial chordae has become our standard procedure to prevent functional mitral stenosis. Further standardization of surgical techniques may contribute to improve long-term outcomes.
journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
title: [Long-term Outcomes and Treatment Strategies for Minimally Invasive Mitral Valve Repair].

abstract: Robotic mitral valve repair (RMVr) may offer a durable and less invasive treatment option for elderly patients with degenerative mitral regurgitation in the era of expanding transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (TEER). We retrospectively reviewed 42 consecutive octogenarians who underwent RMVr for degenerative mitral regurgitation between June 2018 and May 2025. Mean age was 83.0±2.5 years, and 38.1% had preoperative atrial fibrillation. Hospital mortality was 2.4%, and symptomatic stroke occurred in 2.4%. There were no conversions to sternotomy, re-explorations for bleeding, valve reinterventions, or new renal replacement therapy. At discharge, mitral regurgitation was none or trivial in 90.5% of patients, and only one patient had moderate residual regurgitation. Estimated 5-year overall survival was 80.3%, freedom from reoperation was 100%, and freedom from recurrent moderate or greater mitral regurgitation was 89.3%. RMVr was feasible and provided acceptable midterm durability in carefully selected octogenarians. RMVr should remain an important treatment option within multidisciplinary heart team decision-making.
journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
title: [Outcomes of Robotic Mitral Valve Repair in Patients Aged 80 Years and Older with Degenerative Mitral Regurgitation].

abstract: We performed minimally invasive cardiac surgery for mitral repair (MICS-MP) in 386 of 612 consecutive MICS patients (63.1%) from August 2010 to December 2025 using an exoscope-assisted approach. Hospital mortality was 0.8%.Freedom from reoperation was 96.6% at a median follow-up of 75 months, and 92.3% of patients maintained mild-or-less mitral regurgitation at final echocardiographic follow-up. We present our standardized protocol covering preoperative selection, perfusion thresholds, a 5-step repair algorithm, and a 4-stage step-by-step training program, providing a reproducible framework for safe MICS-MP.
journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
title: [Standardization and Education in Minimally Invasive Mitral Valve Repair].

abstract: Persistent left superior vena cava (PLSVC) is an anomaly of the systemic venous system caused by the failure of regression of the left anterior cardinal vein during embryonic development. The patient was a 76-year-old woman, who presented with dyspnea. Echocardiography revealed aortic regurgitation, mitral regurgitation, and tricuspid regurgitation. Computed tomography (CT) revealed an aortic root aneurysm and PLSVC. During the operation, by directly inserting an additional venous cannula into the PLSVC and snaring the cannula, we were able to secure a satisfactory bloodless surgical field and provide adequate myocardial protection.
journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
title: [Bentall Procedure Combined With Mitral Valve Replacement for Aortic Root Aneurysm and Concomitant Valvular Disease Associated With Persistent Left Superior Vena Cava].

abstract: Transcatheter aortic valve implantation by the transaortic approach requires the sheath to be held at a depth of 2 cm. We devised a method to prevent this problem. Cut a gas-sterilized 6 mm inner diameter vinyl chloride artificial heart-lung machine tube to 18.4 cm. Next, a vertical cut is made in the entire length of the tube with scissors. The tube is inserted 2 cm from the tip of the sheath wrapping around the sheath. Once the sheath is inserted 2 cm into the aortic wall, the sheath cannot be inserted any deeper because the tube wrapping around the sheath touches the aortic wall. The sheath can always be lightly pushed against the aortic wall, eliminating the possibility of dislodging. The tube also makes the sheath easier to grasp than the sheath alone.
journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
title: [Contrivance of Holding a Sheath During Transaortic Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation].

abstract: Among 187 patients who underwent coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) between January 2016 and August 2022, 7 patients who received concomitant stent removal and coronary endarterectomy followed by internal thoracic artery (ITA) onlay patch repair were retrospectively reviewed. Six patients were male, with a mean age of 60±12 years;six had diabetes mellitus, and two were on maintenance hemodialysis. All procedures were performed under cardiopulmonary bypass with cardioplegic arrest. The mean number of distal anastomoses was 3.6±1.7, and the mean onlay patch length was 51±13 mm. There was no in-hospital mortality. During a mean follow-up of 52±21 months, one patient died of unknown cause, while no ITA graft occlusion or no new wall motion abnormalities in the left anterior descending artery (LAD) territory were observed. These results suggest that ITA onlay patch repair after long-segment stent removal may be an effective revascularization strategy for diffuse LAD disease with in-stent restenosis.
journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
title: [Onlay Patch Repair Using the Internal Thoracic Artery for Diffuse Left Anterior Descending Artery Disease With In-stent Restenosis].

abstract: A 64-year-old man with medical histories of diabetes, hypertension, and Basedow's disease complained of dyspnea on effort and lower-extremity edema. The patient underwent mitral valve repair and tricuspid annuloplasty for severe regurgitation, cryoablation (Cox-maze IV) and left atrial-appendage closure for atrial fibrillation, and coronary artery bypass grafting to the left anterior-descending branch using the left internal-thoracic artery. Cardiopulmonary bypass was unable to be weaned, and transesophageal echocardiography revealed inferolateral wall-motion impairment. After aortic re-clamping, additional bypass grafting to the posterior descending branch using the great saphenous vein was performed. The wall motion was slightly improved, and cardiopulmonary bypass could be weaned using intraaortic balloon pumping. Coronary angiography was performed immediately after the surgery and detected diffuse right coronary artery spasm. Isosorbide dinitrate was directly injected into the right coronary artery, and the spasm was improved. Bypass grafting for coronary artery spasm might be beneficial to increase coronary blood flow.
journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
title: [Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting for Right Coronary Artery Spasm During Mitral Valve Repair With Cryoablation:Report of a Case].

abstract: Performing open-heart surgery in patients with aplastic anemia (AA) presents significant challenges due to hemorrhagic tendency and increased infection risk. We report a successful case of tricuspid annuloplasty (TAP) and right atrial plication in a 76-year-old female with severe tricuspid regurgitation (TR) and right heart failure, complicated by AA. Preoperatively, the patient exhibited marked cardiomegaly [cardio-thoracic ratio (CTR) 81%], a giant right atrium, and severe TR, necessitating strict perioperative hematological management. Granulocyte-colony stimulating factor (G-CSF) was administered, alongside planned platelet and red blood cell transfusions. The surgery proceeded with no postoperative infectious complications. Postoperatively, heart failure symptoms significantly improved [New York Heart Association (NYHA) I], and cardiomegaly ameliorated (CTR 62%) at five months. This case highlights that safe cardiac surgery in AA patients is achievable with meticulous perioperative management.
journal: Kyobu geka. The Japanese journal of thoracic surgery
title: [Tricuspid Annuloplasty for Tricuspid Regurgitation Complicated by Aplastic Anemia:Report of a Case].

abstract: Mitral regurgitation (MR) is one of the most prevalent valvular heart diseases worldwide. Mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) has become the cornerstone percutaneous treatment for both primary and secondary MR; however, its efficacy remains highly anatomy-dependent, with a substantial proportion of patients deemed unsuitable and others experiencing residual or recurrent MR at follow-up. Looking beyond M-TEER, a growing armamentarium of alternative transcatheter strategies has emerged, including transcatheter mitral valve replacement (TMVR) platforms direct and indirect annuloplasty systems, and, more recently, percutaneous chordal replacement/leaflet-based technologies. This review discusses the current evidence supporting TMVR, transcatheter annuloplasty, and emerging leaflet-based strategies, focusing on those technologies most likely to redefine the treatment algorithm for mitral regurgitation over the coming years.
title: Beyond edge-to-edge repair for the percutaneous treatment of mitral valve disease.
Coronary physiology and the choice of revascularisation strategy.

abstract: Primary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is the preferred reperfusion strategy for ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), rapidly restoring coronary blood flow, limiting infarct size, improving survival, and reducing recurrent ischemic events. Advances in interventional techniques and adjunctive therapies have enhanced its safety and efficacy over time, with high rates of successful epicardial reperfusion, however large intracoronary thrombus burden remains a major challenge during primary PCI. Extensive thrombus promotes distal embolization of platelet-fibrin aggregates and atherothrombotic debris, which mechanically occlude the downstream capillary bed during reperfusion triggering microvascular obstruction, inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, and the no-reflow phenomenon. Consequently, restoration of epicardial patency does not always translate into effective myocardial tissue perfusion or myocardial salvage, resulting in larger infarcts and worse clinical outcomes. Contemporary management strategies aim to reduce thrombus burden, preserve microvascular integrity, and improve myocardial salvage through adjunctive pharmacologic therapies, selective mechanical interventions, and optimized procedural techniques. Although routine use of aspiration thrombectomy and many adjunctive intracoronary therapies have not consistently improved clinical outcomes, selective use in carefully chosen patients remains an important component of contemporary practice. Emerging strategies are shifting the focus beyond restoration of epicardial flow toward preservation of the coronary microcirculation. Advances in intracoronary imaging, precision PCI, and therapies targeting inflammation, reperfusion injury, and microvascular dysfunction offer promising opportunities to individualize treatment and further improve outcomes in patients with STEMI and large thrombus burden.

title: The Achilles heel of successful treatment of acute myocardial infarction: Tackling large thrombus burden and no reflow.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Women are known to have worse outcomes than men in acute myocardial infarction. There is increasing evidence that gender discordance between patients and physicians may be a contributing factor to poor outcomes. Whether the gender of the interventional cardiologist influences outcomes in STEMI and whether this varies based on patient gender is unknown. We sought to ascertain whether the gender of the interventional cardiologist has an association with patient outcome.
METHODS: The NCDR CathPCI registry was queried for cases coded as "Primary PCI for STEMI" between April 2018 and March 2025. These cases were stratified by both patient and cardiologist gender. Logistic regression models were performed and sequentially adjusted for patient and hospital characteristics. Outcomes of interest were door to balloon time (DTB), in-hospital mortality, documented non-system reasons for delay, and door-to-door time (DTD) among transferred- in patients.
RESULTS: Among 834,465 primary PCI procedures for STEMI, only 44,335 (5.3%) were performed by female interventionalists. Male interventionalists were more likely to meet DTB standards. Female interventionalists were more likely to document non-system reasons for delay. There was no evidence of influence of operator gender on the outcomes of patients, when stratified by patient gender.
CONCLUSIONS: Female interventionalists performed a small proportion of primary STEMI PCI procedures. Although female interventionalists had lower adjusted odds of achieving DTB < 90 minutes, interventionalist gender was not associated with adjusted in-hospital mortality. These findings were consistent across male and female patient subgroups and highlight persistent differences in selected care-process measures without a corresponding detectable difference in mortality.
title: Practice Patterns and Outcomes of Women Interventional Cardiologists in Treatment of STEMI.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG) targets are selected by angiographic stenosis, whereas percutaneous coronary intervention increasingly relies on functional assessment. Whether quantitative flow ratio (QFR), a wire-free angiography-derived index, relates to graft outcomes is unclear. We examined preoperative QFR and 1-year graft patency.
METHODS: We retrospectively studied 491 patients undergoing isolated CABG at two heart centers, 2006-2019. Investigators blinded to bypass design and outcome measured preoperative QFR in all analyzable major vessels. Protocol angiography assessed 1-year graft status. Generalized estimating equations accounting for within-patient clustering related QFR (per 0.1-unit increment) to graft occlusion, unadjusted and adjusted for target vessel, graft type, age, sex, diabetes, and ejection fraction. Linearity and effect modification by graft type and target territory were assessed.
RESULTS: Median QFR among 1161 analyzable vessels was 0.66 (interquartile range, 0.48-0.80); among 1036 bypassed vessels, higher QFR was associated with greater 1-year graft occlusion risk (unadjusted odds ratio [OR], 1.27; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.15-1.42; adjusted OR, 1.15; 95% CI, 1.04-1.27; p = 0.008). The association was linear (standardized occlusion probability, 8.2% at QFR 0.50; 13.1% at 0.90). Effect modification by target territory was borderline (joint interaction p = 0.025; Holm-adjusted p = 0.050); this exploratory finding requires confirmation. Graft type did not modify the association (p = 0.28).
CONCLUSIONS: Higher preoperative QFR, indicating functionally less significant stenosis, was associated with greater 1-year graft occlusion risk. This hypothesis-generating, group-level association establishes neither causation nor predictive utility for individual grafts. Prospective validation is needed.
title: Association of preoperative quantitative flow ratio with 1-year graft patency after coronary artery bypass grafting: A two-center retrospective cohort study.

abstract: The plaque microenvironment (PME) integrates systemic lipid exposure with local vascular, immune and stromal responses. Vascular smooth muscle cells, endothelial cells, monocytes, macrophages, fibroblast-like cells and lymphocytes interact within a continuously remodeled extracellular matrix. Their context-dependent states influence inflammation, lipid handling, matrix organization and the balance between plaque stability and vulnerability. This narrative review examines these cellular and extracellular components, with particular attention to phenotypic modulation, endothelial-to-mesenchymal transition and the limitations of inferring cellular origin from shared markers. Human single-cell findings expand the conventional M1/M2 view of macrophages. Therapeutic evidence is considered across experimental models, human pathology, intravascular imaging and randomized clinical outcome trials. Systemic lipid lowering and selected anti-inflammatory interventions can modify atherosclerotic disease, but changes in plaque composition do not by themselves establish reductions in myocardial infarction or stroke. Carotid and coronary findings also require site-specific interpretation. Integrating mechanistic observations with the level and anatomical setting of the evidence provides a framework for evaluating established therapies and developing selective PME-directed strategies.
title: The atherosclerotic plaque microenvironment: cellular plasticity, extracellular matrix remodeling, and plaque stability.

abstract: Evidence on concomitant mitral transcatheter edge-to-edge repair (M-TEER) and left atrial appendage closure (LAAC) is limited. This retrospective registry compared 216 isolated M-TEER procedures with 133 concomitant procedures at 13 centers. The primary endpoint was cardiovascular death, stroke or transient ischemic attack, or site-reported major bleeding through 24 months. Analyses used Kaplan-Meier estimates, center-clustered Cox models, and overlap weighting. Median follow-up was 21.5 months after isolated and 9.2 months after concomitant treatment. The primary endpoint occurred in 41 (19.0%) and 16 (12.0%) patients, respectively; 24-month event-free survival was 73.8% and 80.1%. The adjusted hazard ratio was 0.79 (95% confidence interval 0.50-1.25), and the expanded overlap-weighted estimate was 0.79 (0.49-1.28). Overlap-weighted estimates with follow-up truncated at 9 and 12 months were 1.02 (0.56-1.83) and 0.91 (0.50-1.63). Results were sensitive to exclusion of patients with reconstructed event dates. Oral anticoagulation at discharge was prescribed in 187/202 (92.6%) evaluable isolated-procedure patients and 20/133 (15.0%) concomitant-procedure patients; standardized longitudinal medication assessments were unavailable. In conclusion, concomitant M-TEER and LAAC was feasible and associated with less anticoagulant prescription at discharge, but nonrandom allocation, unequal follow-up, incomplete bleeding classification, and uncertain event timing prevent conclusions regarding comparative clinical benefit.
title: Concomitant Mitral Transcatheter Edge-to-Edge Repair and Left Atrial Appendage Closure in Patients With Atrial Fibrillation and High Bleeding Risk.
Effectiveness and major bleeding complications with venoarterial extracorporeal membrane oxygenation in category E pulmonary thromboembolism: a multicentre retrospective study.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: ST-segment elevation decides who undergoes immediate angiography, yet a quarter to a third of patients without it have an occlusion myocardial infarction (OMI) and follow the slower non-ST-elevation pathway. Their outcome over extended follow-up compared with ST-elevation myocardial infarction (STEMI), including non-fatal events, is poorly defined.
METHODS: In a retrospective single-centre cohort, we reclassified 313 consecutive patients with acute coronary syndrome undergoing angiography as STEMI, NSTEMI-OMI, or NSTEMI-non-OMI. OMI was pre-specified as culprit TIMI flow ≤2, and/or markedly elevated peak troponin with a new wall-motion abnormality. The composite of death, recurrent myocardial infarction, or cardiovascular readmission was assessed at 12 months and over a median follow-up of 26.2 months.
RESULTS: Of 313 patients, 177 had STEMI and 136 had no ST-elevation, of whom 54 (39.7%) fulfilled OMI criteria. Median time to angiography was 10.1 h in NSTEMI-OMI versus 1.0 h in STEMI (p < 0.001) and 15.9 h in NSTEMI-non-OMI (p = 0.140). The 12-month composite occurred in 16.7% of NSTEMI-OMI, 3.4% of STEMI, and 2.4% of NSTEMI-non-OMI (p = 0.001). The adjusted hazard ratio for NSTEMI-OMI was 3.46 (95% CI 1.70-7.02) versus STEMI and 3.31 (1.43-7.63) versus NSTEMI-non-OMI. In patients event-free at 12 months, the unadjusted hazard ratio versus STEMI was 3.56 (1.40-9.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Patients with OMI but no ST-segment elevation waited longer for angiography than STEMI and had a higher hazard of the composite outcome than both other groups, an excess persisting beyond the first year.
journal: Cardiovascular revascularization medicine : including molecular interventions
title: Occlusion myocardial infarction without ST-elevation is associated with delayed angiography and a higher risk of cardiovascular events.

abstract: Anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) use has been associated with adverse cardiovascular events, including myocardial infarction. Proposed mechanisms include alterations in hemostasis and fibrinolysis, endothelial dysfunction, and abnormal vascular reactivity, potentially increasing susceptibility to coronary thrombosis. However, establishing a causal relationship in an individual patient requires careful exclusion of alternative etiologies. We report the case of a 45-year-old female fitness coach who presented with acute myocardial infarction following a six-week course of oxandrolone and methenolone in preparation for a bodybuilding competition. She had no conventional cardiovascular risk factors. Electrocardiography showed ST-segment elevation in the inferior leads. Coronary angiography revealed a large non-occlusive thrombus in the mid-right coronary artery with preserved TIMI 3 distal flow and no obstructive coronary artery disease. Optical coherence tomography confirmed a large adherent thrombus without visible intimal rupture. An extensive thrombophilia and autoimmune workup was unremarkable, and no cardiac source of embolism or in-hospital arrhythmia was identified. The temporal relationship with AAS exposure suggested a possible causal link. The patient was managed conservatively with intensive antithrombotic therapy, and follow-up coronary angiography at two months demonstrated complete thrombus resolution. This report highlights the potential association between AAS exposure and acute coronary thrombosis and discusses possible pathophysiological mechanisms, the diagnostic role of intracoronary imaging, and the individualized management of this uncommon presentation.
title: Acute coronary thrombosis following anabolic-androgenic steroid use in a female athlete: A case report.

abstract:
BACKGROUND: Despite increasing transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) activity in Australia in recent years, patient access to TAVI remains limited and is often more complex than access to surgical aortic valve replacement (SAVR). The aim of this study was to identify socioeconomic factors associated with the likelihood of receiving TAVI versus SAVR in New South Wales (NSW), Australia.
METHODS: Data from the NSW Admitted Patient Data Collection were used to compare the clinical and socioeconomic profiles of patients aged ≥65 years who underwent either TAVI or SAVR between 1 November 2017 and 28 February 2022. Multiple logistic regression analyses were performed on the overall patient cohort and on subgroups defined by age groups, hospital type and funding type.
RESULTS: The study included 6,493 patients (mean age: 79.1 years, 35.5% female) who underwent aortic valve replacement (SAVR=3,294; TAVI=3,199). The odds of receiving TAVI versus SAVR increased significantly with age (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] for patients aged 85 years and older versus those aged 75-84 years: 12.3, 95% CI: 9.99-15.2). Patients from the most disadvantaged socioeconomic areas had lower odds of receiving TAVI than those from the least disadvantaged areas (aOR:0.58, 95% CI: 0.47-0.73). Patients with private health insurance/Department of Veterans Affairs (PHI/DVA) funding were more likely to receive TAVI than SAVR (aOR: 3.29, 95% CI: 2.61-4.14), with this finding consistent across age groups and even more pronounced in patients treated in public hospitals (aOR: 5.82, 95% CI: 4.40-7.70).
CONCLUSIONS: Our study highlights significant variations in TAVI access based on age, socioeconomic status of area of residence, and funding type. These findings underscore the need for policy settings that promote equitable access and ensure that procedural choices for aortic valve replacement reflect clinical needs.
title: Variations in Access to Transcatheter Aortic Valve Implantation Versus Surgical Aortic Valve Replacement by Socioeconomic Factors: A Retrospective Population-Level Study in New South Wales, Australia.

abstract: ABSTRACT Fixed obstruction at the aortic isthmus may preclude transfemoral transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR). Covered‐stent implantation can restore large‐bore access, but immediate passage of balloons and delivery systems through a newly implanted stent may expose it to longitudinal traction. Secondary stent migration during withdrawal of a valvuloplasty balloon and its intraluminal balloon‐assisted rescue have not been well characterized. An 87‐year‐old man with New York Heart Association class III symptoms had severe bicuspid aortic stenosis (peak velocity, 4.4 m/s; mean gradient, 48 mmHg; valve area, 0.65 cm2; left ventricular ejection fraction, 55%) and a focal juxtaductal aortic‐isthmus stenosis with a peak‐to‐peak gradient of 32 mmHg. Because of high surgical risk and unfavorable alternative access, same‐session covered‐stent treatment followed by transfemoral TAVR was selected. A 12 × 29‐mm Advanta V12 covered stent was deployed and flared using an 18‐mm noncompliant balloon. After aortic‐valve predilation with a 23‐mm noncompliant balloon, the stent migrated distally during balloon withdrawal. Guidewire access was preserved, and the stent remained coaxial. The balloon was recentered within the migrated stent and partially reinflated, allowing the balloon and stent to be advanced proximally as a single unit. After restoration and re‐expansion of the stent, a 23‐mm Myval valve was implanted successfully. Final transvalvular and isthmic gradients were 8 and 5 mmHg, respectively, with trivial paravalvular regurgitation and no aortic injury. The patient was discharged on day 3 and remained in NYHA class I at 6 months. Withdrawal of a large valvuloplasty balloon may cause secondary migration of a newly implanted aortic‐isthmus stent. When guidewire access, coaxial alignment, and structural integrity are preserved, controlled intraluminal balloon‐assisted repositioning may provide an effective bailout while maintaining transfemoral access.
title: Covered‐Stent Migration During Same‐Session Aortic Isthmus Repair and Bicuspid Aortic Valve TAVR

abstract: Abstract Background Patients with diabetes mellitus (DM) undergoing PCI are at high risk of restenosis and late stent thrombosis. The Firehawk stent (abluminal biodegradable‐polymer sirolimus‐eluting stent [SES]) is designed to minimize inflammation and enhance vascular healing, which may improve outcomes in patients with DM. Aims In this subgroup analysis of the TARGET All Comers trial, we compared 5‐year outcomes of patients based on diabetes status treated with the Firehawk SES versus XIENCE everolimus‐eluting stent (EES). Methods TARGET All Comers randomized patients 1:1 to Firehawk or XIENCE. In this analysis, we compare non‐stratified outcomes in DM versus non‐DM patients overall and based on stent type. The primary end point was target lesion failure (TLF) at 5 years, a composite of cardiac death, target vessel myocardial infarction (TVMI), or ischemia‐driven target lesion revascularization (TLR). Secondary end points included components of the primary outcome and definite/probable stent thrombosis. Results Of the 1651 patients enrolled, 388 (23%) had DM (197 Firehawk and 191 XIENCE) and 1263 (77%) had no DM (624 Firehawk and 639 XIENCE). Patients with DM were older, had more hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and more prior coronary interventions. Compared with non‐DM patients, TLF ( p < 0.001), cardiac death ( p < 0.001), TVMI ( p = 0.002), ischemia‐driven TLR ( p < 0.001), and definite/probable stent thrombosis ( p = 0.008) were more frequent in patients with DM. There were no differences in primary or secondary end points between Firehawk and XIENCE in patients with or without DM. Conclusion This subgroup analysis of the multicenter TARGET All Comers trial shows that at 5 years, the rate of TLF among patients with DM was similar with the Firehawk SES and the XIENCE EES. Our analysis demonstrates that regardless of stent type, patients with DM have higher rates of TLF.
title: Final 5‐Year Results of Abluminal Groove‐Filled Biodegradable‐Polymer Sirolimus‐Eluting Stent Versus Durable‐Polymer Everolimus‐Eluting Stent in Patients With Diabetes: Results of the TARGET AC Trial

abstract: ABSTRACT Background Dual‐lumen microcatheters (DLMs) are adjunctive devices that has been increasingly incorporated into contemporary percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). These catheters contain two independent working lumens, a rapid‐exchange (RX) port and an over‐the‐wire (OTW) port, within a single low‐profile shaft, permitting guidewire advancement and exchange within a shared working space. Published consensus documents have focused predominantly on chronic total occlusion (CTO) lesions, with less on non‐CTO lesions. Methods This narrative review describes five practical applications of DLMs in non‐CTO lesions. For each technique, we outlined the procedural rationale, a stepwise approach, and technical considerations. Results Five applications are presented: (1) aorto‐ostial wiring in the setting of a protruding ostial stent or anomalous coronary takeoff; (2) reverse wiring of a side branch with an acute or angulated takeoff; (3) side‐branch re‐entry after stent deployment; (4) contrast injection through the OTW port; and (5) parallel wiring for complex lesions. Conclusions DLMs offer several practical applications beyond CTO PCI. Familiarity with these techniques and their technical considerations may help operators select and apply DLM‐assisted strategies in complex non‐CTO lesions.
title: Dual‐Lumen Microcatheters in Percutaneous Coronary Intervention: Five Useful Techniques to Facilitate Coronary Wiring in Non‐CTO Lesions

abstract: Management of prehospital hemorrhagic shock and traumatic cardiac arrest remains a critical capability gap in trauma resuscitation. Hybrid endovascular and extracorporeal technologies and techniques are evolving to meet the challenges of noncompressible hemorrhage, tissue perfusion, gas exchange, and metabolic derangement correction in the setting of complex traumatic injuries and aim to improve patient outcomes by augmenting the capabilities of interdisciplinary trauma/critical care resuscitation teams. The clinical value of these emerging technological advancements depends upon matching the intervention(s) to the dominant physiological failure modes while assisting in damage control surgery and definitive surgical repair. This narrative review discusses advancements in resuscitative endovascular balloon occlusion of the aorta (REBOA) and inferior vena cava (REBOVC), selective regional perfusion, and extracorporeal membrane oxygenation (ECMO), and the technical and logistical barriers facing their clinical implementation. An escalating care pathway and conceptual framework to manage noncompressible hemorrhage and hemorrhage-induced traumatic cardiac arrest utilizing an integrated endovascular and extracorporeal approach is proposed based on prior literature and recent developments in selective abdominopelvic perfusion. Market dynamics remain an important consideration for fielding new technologies; development of specialized medical devices would benefit from versatile, multi-use capabilities to serve broader patient populations to enable economically sustainable employment within healthcare systems.
title: Endovascular and Extracorporeal Management of Complex Traumatic Injuries: Emerging Technologies and Techniques

abstract: The current definitions, explanations, and clinical classification of angina pectoris, particularly the traditional definitions of "typical" and “atypical” angina or chest pain and the stable versus unstable dichotomy, contains conceptual inconsistencies that impair understanding concepts, diagnostic clarity and clinical decision-making. This article challenges several long-standing assumptions about angina, especially regarding the "typical angina" construct and unstable angina definition. We argue for a redefinition grounded in pathophysiology of ischemia and clinical logic rather than rigid historical formulas. These criticisms carry important implications for both education and practice.
title: Rethinking Angina Pectoris—Toward Conceptual and Diagnostic Clarity

abstract: Abstract Objective: To investigate the correlation between melanoma inhibitory activity 3 (MIA3) and coronary collateral circulation (CCC) formation in patients with coronary chronic total occlusion (CTO). Methods: A total of 489 patients with CTO admitted to the First Affiliated Hospital of Xinjiang Medical University from January 2021 to July 2022 were enrolled as study subjects. According to the Rentrop classification system, patients were divided into a poor CCC group and a good CCC group. Baseline clinical data were collected, and plasma levels of MIA3 and vascular endothelial growth factor A (VEGFA) were quantitatively measured. Multivariate logistic regression analysis was used to identify independent factors correlated with good CCC formation. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curves were plotted to evaluate the clinical value of predicting good CCC formation. The net reclassification index (NRI) and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI) were calculated to assess the incremental predictive performance of MIA3 when added to traditional risk models. Clinical subgroup and interaction analyses were also performed. Results: Compared with the poor CCC group, patients in the good CCC group showed significantly higher plasma MIA3 levels (1280.87 pg/ml vs.1041.30 pg/ml, P 1462.24pg/ml) was identified as an independent related factor for good CCC formation (OR= 3.152, P Conclusion: MIA3 is an independent protective factor for good CCC formation in patients with CTO. Higher MIA3 levels are correlated with better collateral development, and this association is particularly prominent in patients with dyslipidemia. Incorporating MIA3 into traditional clinical models significantly enhances the predictive performance for good CCC formation in CTO patients.
title: Association Between MIA3 and Coronary Collateral Circulation Formation in Patients with Chronic Total Occlusion

abstract: Abstract Background Patients with cardiometabolic multimorbidity (CMM) undergoing percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) face complex physical, psychosocial, and self-management demands, yet their stage-specific symptoms and care needs across the PCI pathway remain insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to map these stage-specific experiences and construct a patient journey map to inform tailored nursing care. Methods Guided by the Timing It Right (TIR) framework, we conducted a qualitative descriptive study using maximum-variation purposive sampling. Sixteen patients with CMM undergoing PCI were recruited from the Department of Cardiology at a tertiary hospital in Wuhan, China, from June to July 2026 and participated in 20 semi-structured interviews. Qualitative content analysis used four prespecified journey-map domains with inductive development of subthemes, which were synthesized into a patient journey map. Results The PCI pathway was represented by three phases: preprocedural preparation, postprocedural recovery, and transition. Forty-eight subthemes were identified across four domains: symptoms, care needs, emotions, and pain points. Preprocedural accounts emphasized symptom recognition, gaps in chronic disease self-management, and needs for procedural information and reassurance; postprocedural accounts centered on symptom burden, prognostic uncertainty, and rehabilitation support; before discharge, patients anticipated difficulties coordinating multimorbidity self-management and expressed needs for structured, multidisciplinary continuity of care. Conclusions The journey map identified distinct stage-specific patterns in symptoms, emotions, care needs, and pain points among patients with CMM undergoing PCI. These findings may help align nursing support with preprocedural information and reassurance needs, postprocedural symptom and rehabilitation needs, and pre-discharge preparation for coordinated multimorbidity self-management.
title: Symptom-Demand journey map for patients with cardiometabolic multimorbidity undergoing the periprocedural pathway of percutaneous coronary intervention: A qualitative study

abstract: Abstract Background Slow flow/no-reflow after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) is a common complication of acute myocardial infarction (AMI) and is associated with larger infarct size and worse outcomes, yet simple tools for pre-procedural risk estimation remain limited. We investigated whether the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) independently predicts slow flow/no-reflow after PCI in patients with AMI, and whether adding high-sensitivity cardiac troponin I (hs-cTnI) and culprit-vessel location improves prediction. Methods This single-center retrospective study included consecutive patients with AMI who underwent PCI between January 2023 and December 2025. Slow flow/no-reflow was defined as a post-procedural Thrombolysis in Myocardial Infarction (TIMI) flow grade of 2 or less in the culprit vessel. Multivariable logistic regression identified independent risk factors. Discrimination was assessed with the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC); the combined model was compared with NLR alone using paired bootstrap testing of the AUC difference and a nested likelihood-ratio test. Internal validation used bootstrap optimism correction and 10-fold cross-validation. Results Of 305 patients, 53 (17.4%) developed slow flow/no-reflow. Log-transformed NLR (odds ratio [OR] 1.88, 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.22–2.88, P = 0.004) and log-transformed hs-cTnI (OR 1.24, 95% CI 1.01–1.53, P = 0.043) were independent risk factors, whereas a left anterior descending culprit vessel, including the left main, was inversely associated with slow flow/no-reflow (OR 0.44, 95% CI 0.22–0.86, P = 0.016). The combined model achieved an AUC of 0.735 (95% CI 0.659–0.805) versus 0.674 for NLR alone (ΔAUC 0.061, 95% CI 0.003–0.123, P = 0.039); the optimism-corrected AUC was 0.719 and the 10-fold cross-validated AUC 0.722, and calibration was good (Hosmer–Lemeshow P = 0.101). Adding thrombus burden, left ventricular ejection fraction, AMI type, age, or sex did not improve discrimination (ΔAUC ≤ 0.002). Conclusions NLR is an independent risk factor for slow flow/no-reflow after PCI in patients with AMI. Combining NLR with hs-cTnI and culprit-vessel location adds discriminative value that is retained after internal validation. NLR is easy to obtain at admission and may support pre-procedural risk stratification, but external validation is needed before clinical use.
title: Neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio as an independent risk factor for slow flow/no-reflow after percutaneous coronary intervention in patients with acute myocardial infarction: a single-center retrospective cohort study

abstract: Abstract Background: Intravascular lithotripsy (IVL) is an effective treatment for severely calcified coronary lesions during percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI). However, data regarding patient-reported pain and anxiety during IVL are limited. Objective: To compare pain and anxiety levels in patients undergoing IVL-assisted PCI with those undergoing conventional PCI. Methods In this prospective single-center observational study, 100 patients with chronic coronary syndrome undergoing PCI between 2024 and 2025 were enrolled. Fifty patients underwent IVL-assisted PCI and 50 underwent conventional PCI. Pain was assessed using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) and Wong-Baker FACES Pain Rating Scale, while anxiety was assessed using the Subjective Units of Distress Scale (SUDS). Results Baseline demographic characteristics were similar between groups. The IVL group had more complex coronary artery disease, including a higher prevalence of three-vessel disease (70% vs. 38%, p = 0.001), more previous coronary angiographies ( p = 0.007), and higher radiation exposure ( p = 0.018). Despite greater lesion complexity, no significant differences were observed in pain or anxiety scores between groups. The number of IVL pulses was not associated with pain or anxiety. Conclusions IVL-assisted PCI was not associated with increased pain or anxiety compared with conventional PCI despite greater procedural complexity. These findings support IVL as a well-tolerated strategy for the treatment of severely calcified coronary lesions.
title: Pain and Anxiety During Intravascular Lithotripsy-Assisted Percutaneous Coronary Intervention Compared with Conventional PCI: A Prospective Single-Center Observational Study

abstract: Abstract INTRODUCTION Cardiovascular disease remains a leading cause of global morbidity and mortality, with revascularization procedures such as coronary artery bypass grafting and percutaneous coronary intervention being commonly performed interventions. Despite these procedures, patients frequently experience diminished functional capacity and quality of life. Cardiac rehabilitation (CR) is a proven strategy for improving post-surgical outcomes, yet participation remains notably low in low-resource settings such as Pakistan. METHODS This comparative study enrolled 501 post-revascularization patients at a tertiary cardiac care center in Karachi, Pakistan between January 2020 and December 2022. Participants were categorized into attenders (n = 250) who completed ≥ 15 structured CR sessions within 8 weeks, and non-attenders (n = 251) who attended fewer sessions. Exercise capacity was measured using peak metabolic equivalents, while exercise duration was assessed as moderate-to-vigorous physical activity in minutes per week. Assessments were conducted at baseline, 8-week follow-up, and one-year follow-up. Non-parametric statistical tests including Wilcoxon signed-rank and Mann-Whitney U tests were employed for analysis. RESULTS Both groups demonstrated improvements in peak metabolic equivalents and moderate-to-vigorous physical activity from baseline to follow-up. However, CR attenders showed significantly greater median improvements in peak metabolic equivalents (1.41 vs 0.76, p CONCLUSION Structured CR significantly enhances exercise capacity and physical activity duration in post-revascularization patients, with attenders demonstrating substantially greater improvements than non-attenders. These findings underscore the vital role of organized CR in optimizing recovery outcomes in low-resource settings and support the expansion of such programs in Pakistan.
title: Comparative Effectiveness of Cardiac Rehabilitation on Functional Capacity and Physical Activity Duration among Post-Revascularization Patients in a Tertiary Care Setting in Pakistan

abstract: Abstract Background. An intra-aortic balloon pump (IABP) is sometimes needed after coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG), but it is unclear what the timing of that need says about the patient with preserved left ventricular function. Most published series mix different open-heart operations, and the chance of needing support depends partly on the operation. We studied IABP use and timing in one homogeneous group, comparing support already running when the patient left the operating room with rescue support started in the intensive care unit (ICU). Methods. We reviewed consecutive adults who had elective or urgent isolated on-pump CABG with cross-clamping between July 2024 and December 2025, all with a preoperative ejection fraction (EF) of at least 50%. The primary outcome was operative mortality: death during the index stay, or within 30 days. Patients given an IABP were grouped by when it went in and by where support was running: OR-IABP if the balloon was working as the patient came off bypass, ICU-IABP if it started later in the ICU. title: Timing of intra-aortic balloon pump support and early mortality after isolated coronary artery bypass grafting in patients with preserved ejection fraction: a single-centre retrospective cohort study

abstract: Abstract Objective To investigate the association of admission albumin–bilirubin (ALBI) score with long-term major adverse cardiovascular events (MACEs) among patients who survived to discharge after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) for non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction (NSTEMI), and to assess whether ALBI provides prognostic information beyond the admission GRACE score. Methods We retrospectively included 681 patients hospitalized between January 1, 2023, and September 1, 2025, who survived to discharge after PCI for NSTEMI. Patients were categorized into ALBI tertiles (T1, T2 and T3). Kaplan–Meier analysis, multivariable Cox proportional hazards regression and restricted cubic spline analysis were used to evaluate the association between ALBI and long-term MACEs. Missing data were handled using predictive mean matching, generating 50 imputed datasets. Subgroup and sensitivity analyses were performed. The discriminatory performance of the admission GRACE-based model was compared before and after ALBI was added. Follow-up continued through September 6, 2026. Results Among 681 patients, the median follow-up duration was 585 days, during which 186 MACEs occurred, representing 27.3% of the cohort. The cumulative proportions of MACEs in T1, T2 and T3 were 18.1%, 29.1% and 34.8%, respectively, differing significantly among groups (all P
title: Association of the admission albumin–bilirubin score with long-term major adverse cardiovascular events among patients who survived to discharge after percutaneous coronary intervention for non-ST-segment elevation myocardial infarction: a single-center cohort study

abstract: Abstract Myocardial ischaemia-reperfusion injury (MIRI) is a major cause of residual myocardial damage following coronary revascularisation. Unfortunately, effective mechanism-based pharmacological interventions that can be translated into clinical practice remain limited. Emerging evidence indicates that ferroptosis and inflammation mutually reinforce each other and constitute a critical pathological process responsible for the amplification of myocardial injury during the early phase of reperfusion. Upon myocardial reperfusion, ferroptotic cardiomyocytes release damage-associated molecular patterns and disrupt tissue barriers, thereby activating the innate immune system and initiating inflammatory responses. In turn, inflammation promotes oxidative stress, dysregulation of iron metabolism and lipid peroxidation through the activation of inflammatory signaling pathways and the release of pro-inflammatory mediators, ultimately exacerbating ferroptosis. This reciprocal interaction establishes a self-perpetuating vicious cycle that contributes to the progression of MIRI. Encouragingly, several Western medicines and bioactive compounds derived from traditional Chinese medicine have shown therapeutic potential in modulating MIRI. This review systematically summarizes the molecular mechanisms underlying the bidirectional interaction between ferroptosis and inflammation in MIRI and discusses emerging pharmacological strategies targeting this pathological network. Collectively, the available evidence suggests that future therapeutic approaches to MIRI should extend beyond reperfusion therapy, antioxidant treatment, or anti-inflammatory intervention alone and instead consider combined strategies that simultaneously suppress inflammation and ferroptosis. Such an integrated approach may provide a novel translational framework for early risk assessment, therapeutic response prediction and targeted intervention in patients with MIRI.
title: Targeting Ferroptosis-Inflammation Crosstalk: A Novel Strategy for the Prevention and Treatment of Myocardial Ischaemia Reperfusion Injury

abstract: Abstract Background Major adverse cardiovascular events (MACE) continue after percutaneous coronary intervention (PCI) despite advances in revascularisation. Systemic inflammation contributes to atherosclerosis and plaque instability. The Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SII) is an inexpensive, easily calculated biomarker derived from routine blood counts that integrates inflammatory and immune pathways. This study evaluated its prognostic value for MACE after PCI. Methods This single-center retrospective observational study included 400 consecutive adults undergoing PCI for stable angina or acute coronary syndromes over 1 year. Pre-procedural complete blood counts were used to calculate SII [(platelet × neutrophil)/lymphocyte]. The primary outcome was in-hospital MACE, comprising all-cause mortality, non-fatal myocardial infarction, and ischemic stroke. Patients were stratified by SII quartiles. ROC analysis and multivariable logistic regression assessed predictive performance and independent associations. Results MACE occurred in 6.8% (n = 27). SII was significantly higher in patients with MACE than without (1127.19 ± 335.99 vs. 599.92 ± 324.55 ×10⁹/L; p 27) occurred in 72% of the highest versus 1% of the lowest SII quartile (p
title: Prognostic Value of Systemic Immune-Inflammation Index (SIII) in Predicting Major Adverse Cardiac Events (MACE) in Patients Undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI): An Observational Study

abstract: Structured abstractO_ST_ABSBackgroundC_ST_ABSCardiovascular interventions may impact both left ventricular mass (LVM) and end-diastolic volume (EDV), but the net effect on wall thickness has been difficult to accurately evaluate. Global average left ventricular end-diastolic wall thickness (GT) relates non-linearly to LVM and EDV. We hypothesized that if GT is independent of EDV in health, then GT will be an ideal measure of post-intervention change in left ventricular hypertrophy. MethodsGT [mm] was calculated using LVM and EDV by cardiovascular magnetic resonance as previously validated. The correlation between GT and EDV was evaluated in healthy volunteers. Change in GT following intervention was evaluated for aortic stenosis undergoing valve replacement, hypertension commencing antihypertensive medications, athletes undergoing forced detraining, and aortic regurgitation undergoing valve replacement. The performance of GT was compared to LVM/EDV. ResultsAmong healthy volunteers (n=4461, mean{+/-}SD age 59{+/-}10 years, 50% female), EDV correlated with LVM/EDV but negligibly with GT (R2>0.16 vs R2<0.02, p<0.001 for both sexes). GT and not LVM/EDV changed after intervention in all conditions (p[≤]0.02 for all). Post-intervention changes in GT varied by condition (mean{+/-}SEM aortic stenosis [n=102]: -1.75{+/-}0.13mm, hypertension [n=78]: -0.66{+/-}0.08mm, athletes [n=28]: -0.29{+/-}0.09mm, aortic regurgitation [n=58]: +0.50{+/-}0.11 mm, p[≤]0.02 for all comparisons). ConclusionsIn health, GT, unlike LVM/EDV, remains effectively unchanged across EDV values, indicating that GT is a physiological constant in health and can track pathological changes. After intervention, only GT and not LVM/EDV consistently changed. Instead of LVM/EDV, GT should be used to quantify remodelling after interventions in left ventricular hypertrophy.
